records.organization: American Society of Agronomy / Crop Science Society of America / Soil Science Society of America
records.document_title: Statement of Ethics and Code of Conduct
records.notes: Code of Conduct approved December 2025 by ASA, CSSA, SSSA Boards; Statement of Ethics (2024) is foundational document. Both required as condition of membership. Ethics Committee will detail investigation process in 2026.

records.organization: American Registry of Professional Animal Scientists
records.notes: ARPAS is the professional certification affiliate of the American Society of Animal Science (ASAS). Code of ethics is mandatory for board certification. Covers livestock, poultry, and companion animal science professionals.

records.document_title: IFA Members' Commitments / 12 Safety, Health and Environment Principles
records.notes: Protect & Sustain Certification (2012) is the de facto global product stewardship standard. 12 SHE Principles adopted by all IFA members. Covers safety, health, environment, anti-corruption.

records.organization: IFOAM — Organics International (International Federation of Organic Agriculture Movements)
records.notes: Four principles: Health, Ecology, Fairness, Care. Adopted by IFOAM General Assembly September 25, 2005. Explicitly normative/ethical framework underpinning global organic agriculture movement. Implemented through national certification standards.

records.organization: National FFA Organization (Future Farmers of America)
records.notes: 9-pledge code adopted by delegates at 1952 National FFA Convention. Covers courtesy, honesty, respect, sportsmanship, FFA program participation. Chapter-level enforcement. FFA represents ~700,000 agricultural youth members.

records.document_title: Code of Practice on Safety and Health in Agriculture
records.notes: Adopted by international expert group October 2010; endorsed by ILO Governing Body March 2011. Complements Safety and Health in Agriculture Convention C184 (2001) and Recommendation R192. Covers 26 topics. Agriculture employs ~1 billion workers worldwide.

records.document_title: Fair Chase Statement and Hunter and Conservation Ethics
records.notes: Fair Chase concept originates from 5th article of B&C constitution (1888), the earliest known use of the term. Modern statement defines fair chase as ethical, sportsmanlike, lawful pursuit not giving improper advantage over game. Signed affidavit required for trophy record submissions.

Bowhunting-specific application of fair chase ethics. Defines fair chase as ethical, sportsmanlike, lawful pursuit not giving improper/unfair advantage. Takes strong stance against certain technologies (remote scouting, real-time GPS tracking). Fair Chase Affidavit required for records submission.

Adopted by member referendum November 3, 2000; replaced code from 1976 (amended 1986, 1992). Four core pledges: Service and Stewardship, Sound Science, Honesty and Integrity, Communication and Transparency. Bylaws specify reprimand, censure, expulsion as possible sanctions.

First adopted 1976; revised 1992, 2015. 28 canons covering relationships with clients, employers, public, and other foresters. All membership categories required to abide as condition of membership. Complaint procedures via ACF National Office.

ICF received Royal Charter 1982; only UK body conferring Chartered Forester and Chartered Arboriculturist titles. Code of Conduct 2015. Binding on all members with CPD obligations. Emphasizes competence, integrity, trust, and public safety.

records.document_title: FSC Principles and Criteria for Forest Stewardship
records.notes: 10 Principles covering legal compliance, worker wellbeing, Indigenous peoples' rights, community relations, forest management, environmental values, management plan, monitoring, high conservation values, plantation management. Third-party certification; FSC trademark requires compliance. ~200M ha globally certified.

records.organization: Programme for the Endorsement of Forest Certification
records.notes: World's largest forest certification system (~300M ha). Endorses 48 national/regional systems. Three sustainability pillars: ecological, social responsibility, economic viability. Particularly serves small and family forest owners. Third-party assessment against PEFC Sustainability Benchmarks.

Covers responsibilities to aquatic resources, public, employers, peers, and the profession. Includes provisions on scientific misconduct, coercion by employers, diversity and inclusion. Misconduct reported to Executive Director, AFS President, and/or Ethics and Professional Conduct Committee. Also has separate Meetings Code of Conduct.

records.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
records.document_title: Code of Conduct for Responsible Fisheries
records.notes: Adopted by FAO Conference Resolution 4/95 on October 31, 1995. Voluntary but most cited global fisheries ethics instrument. Global and comprehensive scope. Underpins 4 international plans of action, 2 strategies, 28 technical guidelines. Covers conservation, management, fishing operations, aquaculture, post-harvest practices, trade, research.

Current version: 3.1 (July 2024). Three principles: Sustainable Fish Stocks, Minimal Environmental Impact, Effective Management. 28 performance indicators scored 0-100 (80+ = certification). Voluntary application; MSC ecolabel conditioned on certification. Most widely recognized sustainable seafood standard.

Adopted 2007; entered into force November 16, 2017. Applies to all fishers on commercial fishing vessels. Covers: minimum age, work agreements, accommodation and food, medical care, working time, repatriation, social protection, occupational safety and health. Legally binding for ratifying states.

Mandatory for all Registered Members. First responsibility is community welfare, health, and safety. 8+ clauses covering professional reputation, legal compliance (including SEC regulations), and ethical conduct. Separate Code of Conduct for events/community.

records.organization: Australasian Institute of Mining and Metallurgy
records.document_title: Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct Regulations
records.notes: All AusIMM members must comply. Professional Standards Compliance Process (PSCP) enforces accountability. Includes separate Code for Consultants. JORC (mineral resources reporting) and VALMIN (valuation) codes set technical standards. Peak body and trusted voice for Australian resources sector.

records.organization: Institute of Materials, Minerals and Mining
records.notes: Approved by Trustees per Royal Charter. Members must behave honourably, be truthful/honest with clients/colleagues. Public good overrides client obligations. Includes Whistleblowing Guide and Equity/Diversity/Inclusion guidance. Regulates Chartered professionals (CEng, CGeol, CSci, etc.).

records.document_title: Code of Professional Conduct for Members
records.notes: Preamble + Fundamental Principle + 12 Canons. Covers competency, honesty, ethics, conflicts of interest, public health and safety, environmental impact, anti-bribery/corruption, observance of law. Revised 2014. One of the most comprehensive petroleum engineering ethics documents.

October 2013 version. AAPG has 38,000+ members in 100+ countries. Members shall not use AAPG membership to imply endorsement of specific projects. Violation subject to disciplinary action per Bylaws. Covers geological practice in relation to petroleum, natural gas, and subsurface fluids.

Three-tier structure: Canons (broad principles), Ethical Standards (aspirational goals), Rules of Conduct (mandatory). Compliance with Rules of Conduct mandatory; violation grounds for disciplinary action up to membership termination. Covers personal integrity, public welfare, honesty in communication.

records.document_title: Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct
records.notes: Approved by GSA Council September 2019 — first enforceable ethics code in GSA history. Includes mandatory standards and aspirational standards. Covers research misconduct, discrimination, harassment, bullying. 15 formal complaints received since 2019; 6 resulting in sanctions. Also applies to award recipients.

Applies to all Fellows irrespective of grade or whether acting professionally or personally. Incorporates American Geosciences Institute Guidelines and Science Council Guidelines for Chartered Scientists. Council may remove Fellow for serious breach. Covers professional practice integrity, public interest, and safe/welcoming events environment.

records.document_title: Scientific Integrity and Professional Ethics Policy
records.notes: Adopted 2017; updated 2023. Based on Singapore Statement on Research Integrity (2010). Identifies harassment, discrimination, and bullying as scientific misconduct. Applies to all AGU members, staff, volunteers, and non-members in AGU activities. Sanctions mechanisms in place. Relevant to geological/geophysical work in mining and petroleum.

records.organization: Canadian Institute of Mining, Metallurgy and Petroleum
records.document_title: Code of Conduct / Professional Standards for Qualified Persons
records.notes: Members must observe standards of business and personal ethics; demonstrate honesty and integrity; comply with applicable laws and policies. Whistleblower policy; no retaliation protections. Qualified Person (QP) professional standing provides legal accountability for public mineral disclosures. CIM standards incorporated into NI 43-101 (Canadian securities law).

records.organization: International Council on Mining and Metals
records.profession_name: Mining and metals industry executive / company
records.notes: Founded 2001; 10 Principles published 2003; updated periodically. Principles: Ethical Business, Decision Making, Human Rights, Risk Management, Health & Safety, Environmental Performance, Conservation of Biodiversity, Responsible Production, Social Performance, Stakeholder Engagement. Mandatory for all 27 company members (represent ~1/3 of global mining/metals). Annual assurance reporting required. CEO-led organization.

records.document_title: Towards Sustainable Mining (TSM) — Guiding Principles and 8 Protocols
records.notes: Established 2004. First mining standard requiring site-level reporting with external verification. 8 protocols, 30 sustainability performance indicators. Annual self-assessment mandatory for MAC members (Canadian operations); external verification every 3 years. Multi-stakeholder Community of Interest (COI) Panel oversees development. Adopted by mining associations in 13+ countries.

Every WCA member is signatory to the RCP. Principles cover social/economic responsibility, integrity, climate change/emissions mitigation, environmental protection, biodiversity. WCA rebranded to FutureCoal in November 2023 with new Sustainable Coal Stewardship (SCS) framework.

records.document_title: API Auditor Code of Ethics and Conduct
records.profession_name: Petroleum industry professional / API certification participant
records.notes: Applies to all API certification program participants (applicants and licensed/certified organizations and their employees). Covers: legal compliance, conflict of interest disclosure, confidentiality, anti-harassment. Non-compliance may result in withdrawal of application or license/certificate termination.

Principles agreed 2003 (Lancaster House Conference). EITI Standard 2019 replaced EITI Rules (2011). 57 member countries. Requires disclosure of licenses, contracts, beneficial ownership, production volumes, payments, revenue allocation. Anti-corruption and accountability as core ethics content. Not a professional code but a governance ethics standard.

records.document_title: Responsible Mining Standard (Workers' Rights Component) / Charter of Solidarity
records.notes: IndustriALL founded 2012. Represents 50M+ workers in 140+ countries in mining, energy, and manufacturing. Responsible Mining Standard tool supports unions and communities to protect workers' rights. Covers: collective bargaining rights, freedom of association, living wages, maternity leave, health/safety, grievance mechanisms, anti-child labour. Charter of Solidarity addresses corporate violations.

records.document_title: Safety and Health in Mines Convention C176 (1995) and Code of Practice on Safety and Health in Underground Coal Mines (2006)
records.profession_name: Mine worker / mine operator / mining company
records.notes: C176 (1995) is legally binding for ratifying states. Covers: risk notification, mine design, safe operation, emergency procedures, occupational health, worker rights in mines. Supplemented by Code of Practice on Underground Coal Mines (2006) and Code of Practice on Opencast Mines (2018, see below).

records.document_title: Code of Practice on Safety and Health in Opencast Mines
records.profession_name: Opencast / surface mine worker and operator
records.notes: Revised 2018 (original 1991). 11 chapters covering: purpose/objectives, stakeholder duties, safety and health committees, fundamental principles (including risk assessment and OSH management), specific hazards, general controls, work organization. Reflects changes in industry including interaction between large-scale and artisanal mining, and automated machinery. Supplements C176.
IFT is the primary US professional body for food science. Code guides members to consider public benefit, food safety, environmental impacts, and confine advocacy to areas of competence.

records.organization: Institute of Food Science and Technology
records.notes: UK equivalent of IFT. Disciplinary process includes possible expulsion. Also cross-listed in IIT Ethics Codes Collection (node/5093). Companion: Guidelines for Ethical and Professional Practices for Sensory Analysis of Foods.

records.document_title: Code of Ethics for Food Science and Technology Professionals
records.notes: European food science education network. Explicitly designed as a teaching tool. Key principles: honesty, dignity, conflict-of-interest declaration, confidentiality, professional competence.

records.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization / World Health Organization
records.document_title: FAO Expert Consultation on Food Safety: Science and Ethics (Report)
records.notes: Expert consultation held September 2002, report published 2003. Establishes ethical principles for food safety risk analysis: beneficence, non-maleficence, justice, autonomy, transparency, accountability, participation. Relevant to Codex Alimentarius framework.

records.document_title: Occupational Safety and Health in the Food and Drink Industries
records.profession_name: Food and Drink Industry Workers and Employers
records.notes: ILO sectoral working paper / OSH guidance for food, drink, and tobacco sector. Addresses ergonomics, hazardous substances, biological hazards, machine safety. Developed following ILO Food and Drink Industries Committee resolutions. Also covers Division 11 and 12.

records.document_title: Code of Conduct (2020) and Marketing and Advertising Code (2008)
records.notes: Code adopted August 6, 2020. Covers: ethical conduct, lawful cooperation, anti-discrimination, responsible consumption, anti-harassment. Complaint panel includes employment law, DEI, and alcohol beverage law experts. Marketing Code (2008) allows member complaints against other members.

State-level guild ethics code. Commits members to community support, ethical business practices, principles of excellence, equity, and respect. Reinforced through DEI training access. Included as representative of regional craft beverage ethics codes.

Established 1949; continuously updated. Cited as model of effective self-regulation by industry observers. Covers: prohibition of depicting intoxication, no appeals to minors, responsible consumption messaging. 2014 Digital Marketing Guidelines added. FTC has commended the Code.

records.organization: Distilled Spirits Council of the United States
records.document_title: Code of Responsible Practices for Beverage Alcohol Advertising and Marketing
records.notes: 2022 edition. Covers spirits, malt beverages, and wine. Code Review Board adjudicates complaints. 100% member compliance record; FTC-commended. Raises adult audience placement standard to 73.8%. Includes new informal inquiry pathway added in 2022 revision.

records.document_title: WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control (FCTC)
records.notes: Adopted by World Health Assembly May 21, 2003; entered into force February 27, 2005. 38 articles. Ethically significant provisions: Article 5.3 (protect public health from industry interference), Article 17 (economically viable alternatives for tobacco workers/growers). Governs the sector externally rather than being an industry self-code.

records.organization: CORESTA (Cooperation Centre for Scientific Research Relative to Tobacco)
records.document_title: Best Practices and Guidelines for Research on Tobacco and Nicotine Containing Products
records.notes: CORESTA founded 1956. Primary outputs are test methods and research guidelines (CROM best practices). ISO TC/126 liaison. No standalone code of ethics found; research standards imply scientific integrity principles. Included as closest available document for this division.

23% of global cotton production as of 2024. Key ethical provisions: prohibition of child labor (<15), prohibition of forced labor, non-discrimination, freedom of association, minimum wage, safe conditions. Prohibition of Highly Hazardous Pesticides (HHPs). Third-party field verification.

records.document_title: Workplace Code of Conduct and Compliance Benchmarks
records.notes: Based on ILO standards. ~75% of FLA-audited factories are apparel. Covers: prohibition of forced/child labor, no harassment/abuse, no discrimination, freedom of association, compensation, working hours, health and safety. Independent accreditation process. Also covers Divisions 13 and 15.

Dutch NGO founded 1999. 8-point code rooted in UN and ILO standards. Covers: fair wages, reasonable hours, safe/healthy environments, elimination of child labor, freedom of association. Annual Brand Performance Checks publicly reported. Living wages program.

World's largest independent apparel certification program. 12 principles: labor rights (child/forced labor, H&S, harassment, discrimination, hours, compensation, freedom of association), environment, customs compliance, security. Based on ILO conventions. Accepted by Walmart, Disney, Costco, etc. Also covers Divisions 13 and 15.

records.document_title: Business Social Compliance Initiative (BSCI) Code of Conduct 2.0
records.notes: Founded 2003. 11 elements including: workers involvement/protection, freedom of association, non-discrimination, fair remuneration, decent working hours, health and safety, prohibition of child/forced labor, environment, and ethical business behavior. Grounded in UDHR, UNGP, ILO, OECD Guidelines, UN Global Compact. Biennial audit validity. Also covers Divisions 13, 15, 16.

AAFA is the primary US trade group for apparel and footwear. THREADS Protocol is their sustainability and social responsibility policy framework for regulatory engagement. Official CSR partner: WRAP. Social Responsibility Committee coordinates industry best practice sharing. No standalone ethics document found.

records.organization: IndustriALL Global Union / UNI Global Union
records.document_title: International Accord for Health and Safety in the Textile and Garment Industry (2021)
records.notes: Successor to the 2013 Bangladesh Accord (post-Rana Plaza). 200+ brands signed. Covers: freedom of association, independent safety inspections, worker complaint mechanism, safety committee training. Legally binding. Expanding to Pakistan and other countries. Also covers Division 13.

records.document_title: Code of Practice on Safety and Health in Textiles, Clothing, Leather and Footwear (2021)
records.profession_name: Textiles / Clothing / Leather / Footwear Workers and Employers
records.notes: First-ever ILO code of practice for this sector. Adopted October 2021. Covers 60+ million workers. Addresses biological hazards, hazardous substances, ergonomics, physical hazards, machine/equipment safety, building and fire safety. Worker participation as 'essential element.' Also covers Divisions 13 and 15.

records.document_title: LWG Audit Standard (Protocol 7) / LWG Sustainability System
records.notes: Founded 2005. 400+ stakeholders. Protocol 7 introduced social compliance as a non-critical scoring section in 2021; being elevated to critical in next update. Forthcoming LWG Sustainability System adds Manufacturing Standard, Chain of Custody, and Deforestation Due Diligence. Gold/Silver/Bronze/Audited ratings. Covers bovine, caprine, porcine, ovine leathers.

records.document_title: FSC Principles and Criteria for Forest Stewardship (FSC-STD-01-001 v5-2)
records.profession_name: Forest Manager / Wood Products Supply Chain
records.notes: 10 Principles, 70 Criteria. Ethical dimensions: Principle 2 (worker wellbeing), Principle 3 (Indigenous Peoples' legal/customary rights), Principle 4 (local community wellbeing), Principle 6 (ecosystem services). ISEAL Code of Good Practice compliant since 2006. Cross-listed with Division 17 (paper products).

records.profession_name: Forest Manager / Wood Products Supply Chain
records.notes: Originally established by AF&PA in 1994; spun off as independent 2010. World's largest single forest certification standard by area. 13 Principles, 15 Objectives, 37 Performance Measures, 101 Indicators. Key ethical aspects: land stewardship ethic, Indigenous Peoples' rights, community involvement, biodiversity protection. PEFC-endorsed. Cross-listed with Division 17.

records.organization: Technical Association of the Pulp and Paper Industry
records.profession_name: Pulp, Paper, and Converting Industry Professional
records.notes: ~14,000 members globally. Code covers: fair treatment of employees, avoiding unauthorized intrusion into competitors' business, cooperative knowledge sharing, honest assessment of client/employer work, integrity in technical publications (no exaggeration/misrepresentation). Contact: Mary Beth Cornell, mcornell@tappi.org.

Result of merger of Printing Industries of America (PIA) and SGIA. Code covers: upholding highest ethical standards, paramount public safety and welfare, professional honor/integrity/dignity, non-discrimination (race, sex/gender identity, religion, disability, etc.), intellectual tolerance. Enforcement: reprimand or loss of membership/volunteer role.

records.document_title: Ethical Responsibility and Professional and Personal Conduct Code
records.notes: Applies to AFPM members and non-member attendees at AFPM meetings. Requirements: antitrust compliance, adherence to federal/state law, highest professional/ethical behavior, working to build public confidence in refining/petrochemical industries. First offense: informal censure by Executive Committee. Continued violations: expulsion from AFPM (Board of Directors). Downstream/refining counterpart to API (captured in ISIC Section B).

records.document_title: The Chemical Professional's Code of Conduct
records.notes: Approved by ACS Council March 16, 1994; most recently updated August 28, 2019. Replaces The Chemist's Creed (1965). Covers obligations to public, science, profession, employers, students, and personal conduct.

records.document_title: RSC Code of Conduct and Guide to Ethics
records.notes: Binding on all RSC members at Associate Member grade and above; applicants must sign commitment on admission. References The Hague Ethical Guidelines. Separate Guide to Ethics provides detailed guidance.

records.document_title: Working Party on Ethics in Chemistry — Ethical Guidelines and Code of Chemical Ethos
records.notes: EuChemS Working Party elaborates codes of conduct and approaches to good scientific practice and chemical ethos. Covers internal (research integrity) and external (dual-use, sustainability, science policy) responsibilities.

records.organization: International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry
records.document_title: IUPAC Guiding Principles of Responsible Chemistry
records.notes: Eight guiding principles for responsible chemistry: transparency, equity, accountability, sustainability, systems thinking, long-term impact, stakeholder engagement, ethical responsibility integration. Endorsed The Hague Ethical Guidelines in 2016.

records.organization: Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons
records.notes: Developed 2015 by OPCW-convened experts from 24 countries. Endorsed by IUPAC, ICCA, and ICTA. Focuses on dual-use awareness, peaceful applications, Chemical Weapons Convention compliance. Now referenced in RSC Code of Conduct.

records.document_title: Responsible Care — Guiding Principles and Codes of Management Practice
records.notes: Launched in US by ACC (then CMA) in 1988. Membership condition for all ACC members. Seven Codes of Management Practice covering community awareness, pollution prevention, process safety, distribution, employee health, product stewardship, security. CEO-level commitment required.

records.document_title: Responsible Care Europe — Voluntary Management Framework
records.notes: Cefic adopted Responsible Care in 1985. Developed voluntary Responsible Care Management Framework aligning to highest industry standards and sustainability principles. Membership condition for Cefic members.

Established at 2006 International Conference on Chemicals Management. CEO-level commitment by signatory companies. 64 national chemical associations implement nationally. Global Product Strategy also launched at same time. Endorsed by IUPAC and ICTA.

records.organization: Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America
records.document_title: Code on Interactions with Health Care Professionals
records.notes: First published 2002; revised 2009, 2019, and 2022 (effective January 2022). Governs pharmaceutical company marketing to physicians. Prohibits entertainment, luxury venue events, direct gifts. Covers CME support, speaker programs, and consulting arrangements.

records.organization: International Federation of Pharmaceutical Manufacturers & Associations
records.notes: First created 1981; major revision 2019. Covers HCP interactions, gifts, CME, clinical trial transparency, and patient organization relationships. Includes prohibition on gifts to HCPs. Supplemented by Ethoscope open-source guidance resource.

records.organization: European Federation of Pharmaceutical Industries and Associations
records.notes: 2019 consolidated edition replaces separate codes on HCP promotion and patient organization interactions. Covers traditional and digital communications. Embodies IFPMA Code principles. Binding on EFPIA member companies.

records.organization: Association of the British Pharmaceutical Industry
records.document_title: Code of Practice for the Pharmaceutical Industry (2024 Edition)
records.notes: First adopted 1958; 2024 edition in force from 1 October 2024. Administered by the independent Prescription Medicines Code of Practice Authority (PMCPA). Covers prescription medicine promotion to HCPs, patient information, speaker programs, and transparency.

Effective September 1, 2018; unanimously endorsed by AAM Board. Covers generic and biosimilar manufacturers. Distinctive for emphasizing patient access and market competition as ethical values. Covers medicine safety, HCP interactions, and clinical trials.

Adopted by BIO Board of Directors. Covers responsible biotechnology development, informed consent, health and safety priority, science-based regulation, and patient access. Supplemented by BIO Membership Compact & Social Responsibilities.

records.document_title: Code of Ethics and Publication Ethics Policy
records.notes: Covers members, journal authors, reviewers, and conference participants. Emphasizes research integrity (no fabrication, falsification, plagiarism), proper attribution, and non-discrimination. Includes investigation procedures for research misconduct.

records.document_title: Code of Ethics for Certified Welding Inspectors (QC1:2016) and Code of Conduct for Technical Committee Members
records.notes: QC1:2016-AMD1 governs all AWS-certified welding inspectors; public safety paramount. Separate Code of Conduct for Technical Committee Members covers committee participation standards. AWS QC1 certification widely required in US construction, aerospace, and manufacturing.

Applies to all SME-certified professionals. Covers competence, honesty, non-discrimination, confidentiality, conflict of interest disclosure, and societal impact. Explicitly addresses public health, safety, conservation, and environmental issues in manufacturing.

Formerly Electronic Industry Citizenship Coalition (EICC). Founded 2004 by leading electronics companies. Version 8.0 effective January 2024. Five sections: Labor, Health & Safety, Environment, Management Systems, Business Ethics. Third-party audit-verified. 200+ member companies across electronics, retail, auto, toy sectors.

Governs conduct within SEMI activities, events, and committees. Emphasizes professional, respectful working environment free from abuse and harassment. SEMI is the global industry association uniting the entire electronics manufacturing and design supply chain.

records.document_title: Voluntary Ethical Guidelines for Surveillance, Policing, and Semiconductors
records.notes: Addresses responsible semiconductor supply to prevent human rights abuses. Four areas: due diligence, customer relations, development/design, transparency/traceability. Focuses on preventing semiconductor technologies from enabling oppressive surveillance and policing.

records.document_title: SAE International Code of Ethical Conduct
records.notes: Last updated October 26, 2020. Applies to Board members, officers, members, volunteers, staff, vendors, and consultants. Requires lawful, ethical, professional conduct and respectful treatment. Prohibits illegal, dishonest, or unethical actions.

records.organization: American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics
records.notes: Nearly 30,000 members from 91 countries. Key principles: public safety paramount, conflict of interest avoidance, zero tolerance of bribery/fraud, accurate technical reporting, respect and non-discrimination. Formal Ethics Committee with complaint process.

records.organization: International Forum on Business Ethical Conduct
records.document_title: Global Principles of Business Ethics for the Aerospace and Defence Industry
records.notes: Established 2009 by AIA (US) and ASD (Europe); forum launched 2010. Global Principles address: zero tolerance of corruption, use of advisors, conflicts of interest, proprietary information protection. Open to all aerospace/defense companies. Annual conference. 200+ member companies.

records.organization: Institute of Marine Engineering, Science and Technology
records.profession_name: Marine Engineer / Marine Scientist / Marine Technologist
records.notes: Binding on all members at Associate Member (AMIMarEST) grade and above. Covers: competence development, compliance with Royal Charter and bylaws, reporting of violations by other members, notification of criminal convictions. IMarEST is the world's largest multi-disciplinary marine professional body.

records.document_title: AdvaMed Code of Ethics on Interactions with Health Care Professionals (2022/2025 Edition)
records.notes: 2022 revision effective June 1, 2022; updated November 2025 to address data/AI responsibilities. Six cornerstone values: innovation, education, integrity, respect, responsibility, transparency. Covers HCP interactions, training, consulting, speaking arrangements. Includes crosswalk with PhRMA Code.

2024 edition effective January 1, 2025 (supersedes 2019 edition). Mandatory for all RJC commercial members within 2 years of joining; third-party audited. Covers entire jewellery and watch supply chain: mine to retail. Addresses business ethics, human rights, labor, health/safety, environmental performance. Recognized by ICMM as equivalent standard for mining members.

records.organization: Ethical Supply Chain Program (formerly ICTI Ethical Toy Program, formerly ICTI CARE)
records.notes: ICTI Code of Business Practices first established 1995; ICTI CARE Process launched 2002; became ICTI Ethical Toy Program 2018; rebranded Ethical Supply Chain Program 2024. Third-party audited. Covers ~70% of global toy production. Addresses child/forced labor, gender equity, working hours, wages, health/safety, and environmental sustainability.

records.organization: World Federation of the Sporting Goods Industry
records.document_title: WFSGI Code of Conduct — Guiding Principles
records.notes: Model Code of Conduct for sporting goods companies and their suppliers. Based on ILO Conventions and Universal Declaration of Human Rights. Covers forced/child labor, discrimination, freedom of association, wages, working hours, health/safety, and environmental compliance. Members encouraged to adopt own specific code built on these standards.

Paramount principle: safety, health, and welfare of public and fellow workers. Addresses conflicts of interest, professional reputation, fair competition, and continuous development. Enforcement via member conduct mechanisms.

Binds member organizations (not individuals) to transparency, safety culture, prevention of illicit nuclear material use, and compliance with IAEA Safety Standards. All companies must agree upon joining WNA.

records.document_title: Establishing a Code of Ethics for Nuclear Professionals (Nuclear Energy Series guidance)
records.notes: IAEA guidance publication (Nuclear Energy Series) providing a framework for national nuclear organizations to develop their own codes of ethics. Not itself an enforceable code but a standard-setting document.

AGA is a trade group, not a professional association for individuals. Ethics-adjacent document is the Antitrust Compliance Program. No formal member code of ethics for individual professionals was found. Note: 'AGA Code of Ethics' search results often confusingly return the Association of Government Accountants (different organization).

Covers respect, dignity, non-harassment, legal compliance, and protection of organizational assets. Reporting mechanism to Director of Human Resources. AWWA is primarily a technical society; professional ethics framing is lighter than sector-specific bodies.

Standards for honesty of credentials representation, proper product application, marketing accuracy, and public protection. Certification revocation is the enforcement mechanism. Includes marketing guidelines to prevent consumer deception about water quality.

Covers integrity, honesty, professional excellence, collaboration, legal compliance, and accountability. Members align with Engineering Council and Royal Academy of Engineering ethical principles. Commitment made at joining and at every membership renewal.

records.organization: Chartered Institution of Water and Environmental Management
records.document_title: Professional Ethics and Code of Conduct
records.notes: Mandatory for Chartered Water and Environmental Manager (CWEM) status. Members must demonstrate awareness of compliance with the Code. CIWEM runs professional ethics CPD events and maintains an ethics complaint mechanism. Applies to both water (Div 36) and environmental management (Div 39).

Addresses three categories of misconduct: Personal, Professional, and Legal. Requires civility, ethical business conduct, diversity/equity/inclusion support. Supplemented by Event Code of Conduct and Member Association Code of Conduct Toolkit. WEF also maintains standards for water environment professionals through its WEF Sets the Standard program.

Required to be signed before certification application can proceed. Covers legal compliance, honest competition, industry integrity, and faithful professional representation. Focused on decentralized/onsite sewage systems.

records.organization: Solid Waste Association of North America
records.notes: Code of Ethics must be signed before a certification application can begin. SWANA certification covers solid waste managers, operators, and technicians. Separate Code of Conduct available via member community portal.

records.document_title: Code of Ethics and Standards of Practice for Environmental Professionals
records.notes: One of the most comprehensive ethics codes for environmental professionals. Broad view of environment (physical, natural, cultural). Covers data validity responsibility, conflict of interest disclosure, public fidelity, employer loyalty, and non-condoning of misrepresentation. Applies to EIA, remediation, environmental planning professionals.

records.organization: Society of Environmental Toxicology and Chemistry
records.notes: Applies to governance members, employees, members, volunteers, and guests. Principles include scientific integrity, intellectual property respect, avoiding misleading statements, confidentiality, and minimizing environmental effects of research. Supplemented by a separate Code of Conduct.

Members compile/review impact assessments with integrity and impartiality. Covers equity considerations, Indigenous peoples' rights, future generations, and non-advancement of private interests to the public detriment. Also provides FasTips: Ethics and Best Practice Principles of EIA guidance documents.

records.organization: Virginia Section AWWA / Water Works Professionals
records.document_title: Code of Ethics and Standards of Practice for Water Works Professionals
records.notes: State-level AWWA section code of ethics for water works professionals. Cited as a representative example of state-section professional ethics codes that supplement AWWA national Code of Practice.

Adopted December 2000 by AGC of Washington Board; national AGC code adopted by state chapters. Core values: Skill, Responsibility, Integrity. Eight principles including safety above profit and environmental stewardship.

records.document_title: NAHB Code of Ethics / Member Code of Conduct
records.notes: Adherence required for NAHB membership. Enforced by local HBA affiliates. Promotes highest standards of service; prohibits acts bringing building industry into disrepute.

Adopted 1971; reaffirmed 2006 and 2022. Eight principles: performance standards, honest pricing, professional collaboration, selective sourcing, prompt payment, safety leadership, fair compensation, workforce development. Referenced in ABC Bylaws Articles I and III.

Applies to all AIC Members, CACs, and CPCs. Certification renewal requires ethical conduct affirmation. Principles include public interest, no deceptive practices, unbiased advice, continuous learning. Last modified November 2025.

Four foundational principles: Ethical Practice, Professional Excellence, Responsibility to the Public, Program/Project-Centered Practice. CCMs, CACMs, CMITs must affirm at certification renewal. One ethics/safety PDH required since 2021. Zero-tolerance harassment.

October 2015 edition. Covers responsibility to society, sustainable development, knowledge maintenance, due skill and care, Quality-Based Selection (QBS), no fee-based selection influence. PDF: https://fidic.org/sites/default/files/fidic_codeofethics_201510.pdf

Global edition published October 2021; effective February 2, 2022. Five rules based on honesty, integrity, competence, service, respect, and responsibility. Mandatory for all RICS members, candidates, students, and regulated firms. Serious breaches lead to disciplinary action. PDF: https://www.rics.org/content/dam/ricsglobal/documents/standards/2021_roc_en.pdf

Binding on all AIQS members. Covers integrity, professionalism, transparency, CPD requirements, complaint handling. Peak professional standards body for built environment cost professionals with 4,300+ members. PDF: https://www.quantitysurveyors.com.au/images/docs/Code%20of%20Conduct%20-aiqs.com.au_documents_Code%20of%20Conduct%202014.pdf

records.document_title: PMI Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct
records.notes: Effective November 17, 2025. Four core values: Honesty, Responsibility, Respect, Fairness — each with aspirational and mandatory standards. Required for PMP/CAPM certification holders. Ethics complaint process managed by PMI. PDF: https://www.pmi.org/-/media/pmi/documents/public/pdf/ethics/pmi-code-of-ethics.pdf

Published June 22, 2018; last modified June 25, 2019. Ten principles covering professional pride, ethics above business success, honest practices, regulatory compliance, water and energy conservation. Membership requirement.

records.organization: American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air-Conditioning Engineers
records.notes: Adopted 1974; revised 1986, 2007, 2013. Section 1.140.001.1. Eight principles: public welfare, resource stewardship, competence limits, professional care, conflict disclosure, confidentiality, cross-association alignment, cultural respect. Formal Ethics Complaint Form process.

Primarily a community platform/event conduct code rather than a full professional ethics code. Covers civil dialogue, antitrust compliance, copyright respect. Substantive professional ethics come from state licensing boards and ASHRAE.

Formerly PDCA (Painting and Decorating Contractors of America). Standards PDF updated May 2019. Covers professional service, regulatory/insurance/licensing compliance, faithful contract fulfillment, use of industry-standard materials. Membership requires being licensed/registered.

records.document_title: Rules and Regulations of Professional Competence and Conduct
records.notes: Effective January 1, 2018; relaunched after review. Public interest paramount; competence consistent with membership class; integrity at all times; uphold dignity of the Institute. Covers corruption, modern slavery, and crime in construction. Global membership. PDF: https://www.ciob.org/media/498/download
Also covers ATD (American Truck Dealers). Ethics Guide covers four operational areas: sales, service, financial services, advertising. Membership compliance requirement.
Originally published 1947 as NUCDA Code of Ethics; continuously maintained. Covers 38,000+ used vehicle dealers. All members agree to be bound by the code.
Restated February 15, 2022. Wholesale vehicle remarketing industry. Hall of Fame eligibility requires consistent adherence.
Enacted 1970; enforced by independent Code Administrator (not just DSA staff). Binding on all member companies and their salespeople. Consumer complaint mechanism. 2018 compliance edition published.
Updated 2024 (previously 2007 version). Founded 1987. Membership dependent on code adherence. Explicitly requires legal compliance and community service.

Approved October 19, 2002. Five obligation areas: to Family, to Care of Decedent, to Public, to Government, to NFDA. Binding on all member types (Firm, Individual, Retired, Student). Disciplinary action under Constitution and Bylaws.

records.document_title: Code of Ethics and Professional Practices
records.notes: Founded 1962 to promote highest standards of connoisseurship, scholarship, and ethics. Covers dealings with artists, clients, colleagues, and general public. Applies to all transactions including art fairs. Good faith complaint resolution among members expected.

records.document_title: Code of Ethics and Principles of Fair Business Practice
records.notes: Established 1984; 2016 edition most recent PDF. Annual member commitment. Stricter disclosure than FTC minimums. Ethics & Grievance Committee. Covers natural colored gemstones, pearls, natural colored diamonds, colored stone manufactured items.

records.profession_name: Jewellery Supply Chain Professional (mining to retail)
records.notes: 2024 COP effective January 1, 2025. Mandatory third-party certification for all commercial members within 2 years of joining. Covers business ethics, human rights, labor, health/safety, environment. Next revision 2029. Spans Divisions 46 and 47.

records.profession_name: Personal Property Appraiser (Fine and Decorative Arts, Antiques)
records.notes: Established 1949. 900+ members across 100 specialization areas. Requires USPAP compliance. Independence and objectivity are core principles. No outside interest in subject property permitted.

Eight core principles: Integrity, Respect, Fiduciary Responsibility, Compliance, Confidentiality, Loyalty, Duty, Professionalism. Felony conviction in auction work = automatic code violation. Formal grievance process through CEO and Board Chairman. Separate CAI Code of Conduct for certified members.

Founded 1917. Not-for-profit watchdog. Member pledge to comply with all applicable laws and make accurate product representations. Works with FTC, US Customs, State Dept on compliance education. Dispute resolution for consumers and trade. Functions more as watchdog than issuer of standalone ethics document.

records.organization: American Trucking Associations — Moving and Storage Conference
records.document_title: Code of Ethics (Moving and Storage Conference)
records.notes: ATA Moving & Storage Conference division code. Main ATA national body does not publish a general trucking driver code of ethics. This is the most explicit ethics document found for US land transport.

records.profession_name: Public Transit Executive / Transit Agency Officer
records.notes: Applies to APTA officers, directors, and committee chairs. Covers legal compliance, antitrust, meeting conduct, harassment-free environment. Board-approved policy. Not a code for bus drivers or transit workers — governance level only.

records.organization: Nautilus International / RMT / UK Chamber of Shipping
records.document_title: Code of Conduct for the Merchant Navy
records.profession_name: Seafarer / Merchant Navy Officer and Rating
records.notes: Published May 13, 2019. Agreed between Nautilus International, RMT, and UK Chamber of Shipping; approved by the Maritime & Coastguard Agency. Sets disciplinary rules and procedures for seafarers during shipboard employment. Recognizes unique demands of seafaring. Aligned with 2016 MLC amendments on harassment/bullying. PDF: https://alphamarine.ie/assets/PDFs/Code-of-Conduct-for-the-Merchant-Navy.pdf

ILO Convention C186. Entered into force August 20, 2013; amended 2016 (harassment/bullying). Fourth pillar of international maritime law. Covers seafarer rights, working conditions, fair treatment. Code of conduct compliance affects promotion rights. Binding on flag states. Not a professional association ethics code but the primary international normative framework for seafarer conduct.

IMPA Resolutions updated July 2023. No dedicated standalone code of ethics; professional standards expressed through Resolutions and guidance including Master-Pilot Exchange guidance, Diversity and Inclusion Guidance for Pilotage. Public interest served by regulated pilotage free of commercial pressure is a core principle.

records.document_title: Code of Ethics for IMO Personnel
records.notes: Effective date January 1, 2012 (Council adopted as Annex I to Service Code at 193rd Session). Internal staff code, not a seafarer code. Covers loyalty, independence, impartiality, integrity, zero tolerance for fraud/corruption, prohibition on gifts, prohibition on harassment. Applies to all IMO officials. Based on ICSC Standards of Conduct for International Civil Service.

Updated version announced 2024/2025. One of the most comprehensive union-based professional ethics codes in any sector. Canons cover: passenger safety as first responsibility; faithful discharge of duties; command responsibility; conduct on and off duty; no malicious injury to other pilots' reputation; reporting professional incompetence to ALPA. Professional Standards Committee (~500 trained members) processes cases. Represents 79,000+ pilots.

records.document_title: Professional Air Traffic Controller's Code / NATCA Code of Conduct
records.notes: Professional Air Traffic Controller's Code poster (2020) covers: personal commitment to safety and public trust; inspiring professionalism in others; airspace safety as greatest priority; individual actions representing the whole profession. Code of Conduct covers harassment/discrimination-free environment. Professional Standards Committee processes thousands of cases. Controller's Code poster: https://www.natca.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/08/ATC-Code-Poster.pdf

records.organization: International Federation of Air Line Pilots' Associations
records.notes: Represents 160,000+ pilots in 70+ countries. Founded 1948, Montreal-based. Written code focuses on organizational conduct/harassment-free environment at IFALPA events. Professional pilot conduct is deferred to member associations (e.g., ALPA). Safety policies implicitly address ethics. No standalone professional ethics code for in-flight conduct published.

records.organization: Association of Flight Attendants – Communications Workers of America
records.notes: Primarily a union officer ethics code: officers/representatives shall not receive compensation from employer boards; prohibition on personal payments from employers; prohibition on entering management negotiations without MEC President knowledge; prohibition on converting union property to personal use. Operational professional standards handled through EAP/Professional Standards Program.

Applies to all IATA employees and subsidiaries worldwide and, as far as possible, to consultants, contractors, suppliers, and other business partners. Highest standards of ethical conduct and social responsibilities. Not a code governing airline operations or crew conduct — organizational ethics framework for the world's leading airline trade body (representing 290+ airlines).

records.document_title: Aviators Model Code of Conduct (AMCC), Version 3
records.notes: Version 3 released 2022. Peer-reviewed volunteer initiative; endorsed by FAA resources. Covers operating practices to enhance quality and safety; flight and ground safety; professionalism; good judgment, ethical behavior, personal responsibility; improved communication between pilots, regulators, and aviation community. Provided free as public service. Repository: https://repository.fit.edu/amccenglish/

records.document_title: Principles and Standards of Ethical Supply Management Conduct
records.notes: Regularly reviewed by ISM Ethical Standards Committee. Core ethical principles: integrity, value, loyalty. Standards cover: preventing unethical conduct; avoiding conflicts of interest; protecting confidential information; avoiding improper reciprocal agreements; obeying laws and trade agreements; developing professional skills. Applied through ISM certification programs.

records.organization: Chartered Institute of Procurement and Supply
records.notes: 2024 version; significant amendments from 2014 onward. Five commitments: (1) enhance and protect profession standing; (2) maintain highest integrity in business relationships; (3) promote eradication of unethical practices including modern slavery and corruption; (4) enhance professional proficiency; (5) ensure legal compliance. Formal Disciplinary Committee; sanctions range from reprimand to expulsion. Royal Charter authority. Online ethics test since 2014. Professional Register for public verification.

records.organization: Supply Chain Management Association / Supply Chain Canada
records.document_title: SCMA Code of Ethics for Professionals in the Field of Supply Chain Management
records.notes: Reviewed minimum every 5 years. Covers professional judgment, conflict of interest disclosure, no misrepresentation of credentials, compliance with professional standards. Sanctions include reprimand, letter of censure; censured members barred from office for one year. Web: https://scma.com/on/about/code-of-ethics

records.organization: National Customs Brokers and Forwarders Association of America
records.notes: Code embedded within NCBFAA bylaws rather than as standalone published document. Core values: professionalism based on integrity, principles, ethics, and trust. Required adherence for Certified Customs Specialists (CCS). Represents 1,422+ member companies with 110,000 employees. Founded 1897. Bylaws PDF: https://members.ncbfaa.org/4DCGI/cms/review.html?Action=CMS_Document&DocID=8574

records.document_title: Code of Ethics and Professional Standards
records.notes: International organization founded Paris 1929 (Union Internationale des Concierges d'Hotels — UICH). Annual signed oath required. Conflict-of-interest rules (no restaurant commissions). Guest and employer confidentiality. Vendor integrity standards. Motto: 'In Service Through Friendship.'

ALP is the successor organization to PAII (Professional Association of Innkeepers International, est. 1987) + AIHP merger. Aspirational code crafted with association law counsel. All membership categories required to consent. Covers duties to guests, employees, vendors, the Association, and the public.

Policy Manual revised September 2023. Six areas: Ethics and Transparency, Embracing Diversity, Anti-harassment, Business Relationships (no human trafficking), Sustainability. Straddles Div 55 (hotel meetings) and Div 56 (event catering) — classified under 55.

records.document_title: Principles of Professional and Ethical Conduct
records.notes: Represents highest levels of professional and ethical behavior in convention industry. Core principles: integrity, respect, honesty, credibility. Continuing education and knowledge-sharing obligations. Conflict-of-interest avoidance. CMP (Certified Meeting Professional) holders reference this code.

records.profession_name: Business Travel Manager / Corporate Travel Professional
records.notes: National GBTA code implemented at chapter level. Austin chapter document is most publicly accessible. Key provisions: good faith dealings, buyer privacy, fair competition, client confidentiality, professional growth. Violations may result in membership suspension or revocation.

Applies to all full members AND all ACF-certified individuals (CEC, CC, CPC, CCA, CEPC, etc. — multiple certification levels). 20,000+ members. Non-discrimination, safety, professional development, accurate credentials representation. Direct PDF hosted on acfchefs.org.

records.organization: National Association for Catering and Events
records.notes: Formal Ethics Review Procedures with Ethics Complaint Form submitted to ethics@nace.net. Covers inclusion (race, religion, national origin, age, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, political affiliation). Members take responsibility for advancing NACE mission and the profession.

records.document_title: Code of Ethics and Professional Responsibility
records.notes: May 2021 version. Signed as eligibility condition for all CMS-A programming. Core values: Hospitality, Integrity, Humility, Self-Care, Diversity. Diversity and harassment training modules required. Anonymous reporting available. Whistleblower protections.

Core values: Service, Integrity, Sharing Knowledge, Tradition, Camaraderie. Comprehensive anti-discrimination and anti-harassment provisions. Misconduct investigation procedures with membership suspension as remedy. Applies to all in-person and online USBG activities.

Revised 2014 (also 1984, 1987, 1996). Originally 1926 Sigma Delta Chi code. Four principles: Seek Truth and Report It, Minimize Harm, Act Independently, Be Accountable and Transparent. Not legally enforceable under First Amendment; aspirational. Widely taught in journalism schools.

records.document_title: Global Charter of Ethics for Journalists
records.notes: Adopted June 12, 2019 at 30th IFJ World Congress, Tunis. Completes the 1954 Bordeaux Declaration. 16 articles. Based on international human rights law (UDHR). Represents 500,000+ journalists across 140+ countries. Covers truth, source protection, discrimination, editorial independence.

records.document_title: IFJ Declaration of Principles on the Conduct of Journalists (Bordeaux Declaration)
records.notes: First adopted April 1954 at 2nd World Congress, Bordeaux. Amended 1986 at 18th World Congress, Helsingör. Foundational international journalism ethics document. Superseded/complemented by 2019 Global Charter of Ethics. Key principle: respect for truth and public's right to truth is first duty of journalist.

NUJ code first adopted 1936; last revised 2011. Only UK code applying to all types of journalists. Part of union rules as Appendix A. Ethics Council established 1986. All members sign agreement to uphold it. Covers accuracy, honest means, source protection, non-discrimination, conflicts of interest.

records.organization: American Society of News Editors / News Leaders Association
records.notes: Originally 1922 Canons of Journalism; renamed Statement of Principles 1975. Six articles: Responsibility, Freedom of Press, Independence, Truth and Accuracy, Impartiality, Fair Play. ASNE merged with APME to form News Leaders Association. Landmark US journalism ethics document.

APME merged with ASNE to form News Leaders Association. Principles focus on accuracy, public's right to know, independence from conflicts of interest, and correction of errors. Statement of News Values and Principles is the AP's internal standards document widely referenced as industry standard.

Voluntary guidelines presented to the industry by DGA-Employers Creative Rights Committee. Covers director notes, production timelines, post-production, and creative rights. DGA primarily focuses on creative rights protection rather than a traditional ethics code. Ethical obligations are embedded in the guild constitution.

Binding on all WGA members. Violation is grounds for disciplinary action. Prohibits ghost writing, misrepresentation, working for non-signatory producers, and unfair practices. Separate from formal code of ethics; ethical dimensions include anti-fraud, transparency, and fair dealing provisions.

RTDNA (formerly RTNDA) is the primary US professional association for electronic journalism. Code covers accuracy, independence, conflicts of interest, error correction, and incompatibility of commercial endorsements with journalism. Supplemented by coverage guidelines developed by journalists, managers, and subject-area experts.

Approved by BBC Board of Directors. Contractually required for all BBC employees and contractors. Reflects Ofcom Broadcasting Code requirements. Covers accuracy, impartiality, harm and offence, fairness, privacy, and editorial integrity. Widely referenced internationally as the benchmark for broadcast journalism ethics.

Reviewed and approved by CBC/Radio-Canada Board of Directors. Reviewed by two independent experts. Five core principles: accuracy, fairness, balance, impartiality, integrity. Independent ombudsman for public complaints. Applies to news, current affairs, and public affairs content.

records.organization: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers
records.notes: IEEE is the primary professional body for electrical and telecom engineers worldwide (~400,000 members in 160+ countries). Code requires: holding public safety paramount, being honest, avoiding conflicts of interest, treating persons fairly, protecting the biosphere. Applicable to telecom engineers under Division 61.

records.document_title: ACM Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct
records.notes: Revised and adopted June 22, 2018 (previously 1992). Developed over two years with global input. Considered the standard for the computing profession; adopted by many tech companies. Four sections: Fundamental Ethical Principles, Professional Conduct, Leadership Principles, Compliance. Added security-by-design, ML/AI concerns, public infrastructure responsibility.

records.document_title: Software Engineering Code of Ethics and Professional Practice (SE Code)
records.notes: Version 5.2. Jointly approved by ACM and IEEE Computer Society. Standard for teaching and practicing software engineering. Eight SEEEPP principles: Public, Client/Employer, Product, Judgment, Management, Profession, Colleagues, Self (PUBLIC COMPUTER mnemonic). Public interest is paramount.

records.organization: BCS, The Chartered Institute for IT
records.document_title: BCS Code of Conduct for Members
records.notes: Royal Chartered professional body for IT in the UK. Members sign code on joining; professional duty accepted. Disciplinary action can result in expulsion. Four sections: Public Interest, Professional Competence and Integrity, Duty to Relevant Authority, Duty to Profession. Higher standards than general law.

New code launched December 2023. Underpinned by three values: honesty, trustworthiness, respect. Provides ethical decision-making guidance, values/principles for professional conduct, and behaviors that build public trust. Replaces earlier Code of Professional Conduct (v2.1, 2014) which had six core values.

Required condition of ISC2 certification. Four canons: (1) Protect society, common good, infrastructure; (2) Act honorably, honestly, justly, responsibly, legally; (3) Provide diligent and competent service; (4) Advance and protect the profession. Code violations can result in certification revocation. Members expected to report violations.

records.document_title: Code of Professional Conduct for Cybersecurity Professionals
records.notes: Launched February 2026. Builds upon and expands the ISC2 Code of Ethics canons. Broadens scope beyond certification holders to all cybersecurity professionals. Provides practical guidelines for issues encountered in professional work. Represents an evolution from the foundational four canons.

records.profession_name: IT Auditor / IT Governance Professional / Cybersecurity Professional
records.notes: Applies to ISACA members and certification holders (CISA, CISM, CRISC, CGEIT). Seven principles covering: standards compliance, objectivity and due diligence, lawful service, privacy/confidentiality, competency, transparent reporting, and professional education of stakeholders. Non-compliance may result in investigation and disciplinary measures.

Required for all EC-Council certification holders (CEH, CHFI, etc.). Key obligations: no malicious hacking, authorized penetration testing only, protect client confidentiality, no sale of personal data, disclose dangers to public, serve within competency areas, advance professional knowledge. Certification revocation for violations.

IEEE Computer Society is a division of IEEE with specific focus on computing. The IEEE Code of Ethics applies to all IEEE members including computer engineers. Also co-sponsors the SE Code (see ISIC-J62-002). IEEE is the world's largest technical professional organization.

Applies to DAMA officers, advisors, CDMP (Certified Data Management Professional) holders, and members. Principles: integrity, professionalism, honesty, fairness, respect for individual rights. Members must honor proprietary rights of employers and organizations. All DAMA chapters share the code.

ARMA International (information and records management). Three areas: society, employers, profession. Supports free flow of information, accurate information systems, confidentiality, avoidance of conflicts of interest. Also cross-listed under Section P (archivists/librarians) due to overlap.

First code adopted 1950; current version 2000. Three parts: preamble, six professional values (advocacy, honesty, expertise, independence, loyalty, fairness), six code provisions of conduct. Previously enforced with sanctions; now aspirational with member pledge. ~22,000 members.

World's only Royal Chartered professional body for PR practitioners. ~11,000 members commit annually. Four key principles: integrity, competence, transparency, confidentiality. Violations reported to Professional Practices Committee; Disciplinary Committee can impose sanctions up to membership termination. Updated November 2025.

Required for IAB membership. Covers transparency in data collection, security, marketing to children, and compliance. Incorporates Self-Regulatory Principles for Online Behavioral Advertising. Sanction for non-compliance: six-month membership termination. Also has separate Code of Ethics for IAB Certification holders.

records.document_title: ABA Professional Certifications Code of Ethics
records.notes: Applies to holders of ABA professional certifications (CRCM, CTFA, etc.)
BIS-published; G20 and FSB-endorsed. Requires banks to develop written codes of ethics or conduct. Revised July 2015.

records.document_title: Code of Conduct and Work Ethics in Financial Institutions
records.notes: Statutory instrument. Covers banks, insurance companies, finance companies, money exchange centers supervised by SAMA. August 2019.

records.document_title: Code of Ethics for the Financial Services Industry
records.notes: Launched by Bank Negara Malaysia and Securities Commission Malaysia. Five principles: competence, integrity, fairness, confidentiality, objectivity. Covers banking, capital markets, insurance, Islamic finance across Malaysia/Singapore/HK.

records.document_title: Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct
records.notes: Updated 2024 edition adds Standard I(E) Competence. Applies to CFA charterholders, members, and candidates globally. 7 major standards with sub-standards.
Ethical standards for fair representation and full disclosure of investment performance. Adopted in 54+ markets. Voluntary but widely required by institutional clients.

records.document_title: Rule 2010 — Standards of Commercial Honor and Principles of Trade
records.notes: Binding on all FINRA member firms and associated persons. Serves as the broad ethical 'catch-all' standard for US securities industry. Enforced with fines, suspensions, bars.
12 high-level principles. Statutory — breaching PRIN can lead to FCA fines, loss of authorisation. Applies to all FCA-regulated firms across banking, investment, insurance.

records.document_title: Code of Conduct (Lord George Principles, 2021 edition)
records.notes: Eight principles. Shared with the Worshipful Company of International Bankers. Members must pass IntegrityMatters assessment. Also used internationally by CISI members globally.

records.document_title: Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulation (38 Principles)
records.notes: G20 and FSB-endorsed. 38 principles covering securities markets, market intermediaries, issuers, analytical services, and CIS. Used in IMF/World Bank FSAPs. 225 member jurisdictions.

records.document_title: Code of Conduct Fundamentals for Credit Rating Agencies
records.notes: Model code with 50+ provisions. Moody's, S&P, Fitch substantially implemented. Supervised by SEC (US) and ESMA (EU). Addresses conflicts of interest, methodology consistency, disclosure.

records.organization: Securities and Futures Commission of Hong Kong
records.document_title: Code of Conduct for Persons Licensed by or Registered with the SFC
records.notes: Statutory conduct requirements under the Securities and Futures Ordinance. Covers insider dealing prevention, conflict of interest, reporting obligations.

records.document_title: Rules and Enforcement Framework (successor to IIROC/MFDA)
records.profession_name: Investment Dealer / Mutual Fund Dealer Representative
records.notes: CIRO formed Jan 1 2023 from merger of IIROC and MFDA. Inherits IIROC Dealer Member Rules and MFDA Rules. Ethical conduct standards embedded in rulebook.

records.document_title: Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct
records.notes: Revised Dec 2023. All IMAS members must comply. Addresses professionalism, ethical conduct, conflicts of interest for Singapore investment management industry.
Applies to FRM and ERP certification holders, GARP board, regional directors, committee members, staff. Violations can lead to suspension or removal of designation.

Founded 1896 to establish code of ethics for credit management. Requires highest standards of integrity, trust, fairness; confidentiality of credit information. Certification promotes ethical practices.

records.document_title: Standards of Practice / Best Practices for Investment Adviser Code of Ethics
records.notes: Best practices guidance since 1937. Covers fiduciary duty, personal securities transactions, insider trading prohibitions, compensation disclosure. Basis for SEC investment adviser regulations.

records.document_title: CPCU Code of Professional Conduct (Nine Canons)
records.notes: Nine canons covering public interest, fair treatment, business integrity, professional development. Ethics course and exam required for CPCU designation. Can rescind certification for violations.

records.organization: National Association of Insurance and Financial Advisors
records.document_title: Code of Ethics / Ethics for Financial Professionals
records.notes: Updated July 2024 incorporating FSP Code of Professional Responsibility. Requires best interest standard, confidentiality, accurate disclosure. Longest-standing insurance ethics code in US.

records.organization: Independent Insurance Agents & Brokers of America
records.notes: Also known as Big I. Covers fair competition, no misrepresentation, thorough client needs analysis, observance of insurance laws. Member commitment as condition of membership.

records.organization: American Academy of Actuaries / SOA / CAS / CCA / ASEA
records.document_title: Code of Professional Conduct (Unified US Actuarial Code)
records.notes: Jointly adopted by all 5 US actuarial organizations Jan 1 2001. 14 precepts covering honesty, competence, courtesy, conflicts. Enforced by ABCD. Covers all actuarial specialties.
SOA's adoption of the unified US Code. Primary for life, health, pensions actuaries. Enforced through ABCD disciplinary procedures.
CAS adoption of the unified US Code. Primary for property-casualty actuaries. Also maintains separate Code of Professional Ethics for candidates.
Revised version effective Sep 25 2025. Six principles: Integrity, Competence and Care, Impartiality, Compliance, Speaking Up, Communication. Violations lead to IFoA Disciplinary Scheme proceedings.
Effective Jul 1 2025 (previous version Mar 31 2020). Principles-based. Three core principles: Integrity, Compliance, Objectivity. Encompasses all aspects of member's life.

records.document_title: Principles of Professionalism (PG1) / EC Code of Conduct
records.notes: IAA Professionalism Guideline 1 (PG1) sets minimum requirements for member association codes. EC Code of Conduct governs IAA leadership. Supports knowledge, values, accountability framework.
Canadian adoption of the US unified actuarial Code of Professional Conduct. Aligned with IAA Professionalism Guidelines.

records.document_title: Code of Professional Conduct for ARA Members
records.notes: Covers ASPPA, ASEA, NAPA, NTSA, and PSCA members. Identical to unified actuarial Code for actuary members; adds provisions for non-actuary retirement plan consultants.

records.organization: National Conference on Public Employee Retirement Systems
records.document_title: Code of Conduct for Public Pension Service Providers
records.notes: 10 principles for service providers (legal, financial, accounting, investment, custody) to public pension plans. Includes independence, objectivity, conflict disclosure requirements.
CFA Institute voluntary code for pension trustees. Addresses fiduciary duty, loyalty to beneficiaries, prudent investment, conflict management.

records.document_title: Code of Ethics and Standards of Conduct
records.notes: Effective Oct 2019; enforcement began June 2020; updated July 2024. Imposes fiduciary duty at all times when providing Financial Advice. Includes duty of loyalty, care, and to follow client instructions. Binding on all 90,000+ CFP® professionals.

records.organization: National Association of Personal Financial Advisors
records.document_title: Fiduciary Oath and Code of Ethics
records.notes: Fee-only advisors only (no commissions). Three overlapping ethical standards: NAPFA Fiduciary Oath, Advisers Act fiduciary requirements, CFP Standards. No contingent compensation clause is core.

records.document_title: Code of Ethics / Ethics Policies and Procedures
records.notes: FPA members must comply with FPA Code and CFP Board Code. Aspirational in that FPA itself defers enforcement to CFP Board. Principles: integrity, objectivity, competence, fairness, confidentiality.

records.organization: Financial Adviser Standards and Ethics Authority / Financial Advice Association Australia
records.document_title: Financial Planners and Advisers Code of Ethics 2019
records.notes: Legislative instrument F2019L00117 under Corporations Act 2001 s921E. Compliance mandatory from Jan 1 2020. Five values, twelve standards. Highest-level statutory ethics code for financial planners globally. Administered by ASIC.

records.document_title: Code of Ethics for Designated Professionals (CIM®, FCSI®, PFP®, CIWM, MTI®)
records.notes: Multiple designation-specific codes sharing common principles: integrity, honesty, fairness, compliance, respect. Enforced by CSI Designation Ethics Committee with disciplinary sanctions.

records.document_title: Code of Ethics / Lending Integrity Seal Standards
records.notes: Lending Integrity Seal of Approval for members pledging strict code. Requires honesty, accurate advertising, professional conduct. NAMB L.I.S.A. program with grievance review process.

State chapter-adopted canons (MBANJ model widely replicated). Requires candor, fairness, non-discrimination, timely processing, full disclosure of interests, oral agreements accorded same weight as written contracts.

records.document_title: Code of Ethics and Professional Responsibility
records.notes: Specific to reverse mortgage lending (HECMs). Covers elderly client protections, fair dealing, proper counseling referral, compliance with HUD guidelines.

records.document_title: Asset Manager Code of Professional Conduct
records.notes: Firm-level code (distinct from individual CFA Code). Covers loyalty to clients, performance disclosure, risk management, compliance. Voluntary adoption as signal of commitment to ethical management.

records.organization: National Association of Independent Insurance Adjusters
records.notes: 10-point code. Requires unprejudiced investigations, truthful reporting, no improper alliances, equitable billing, no improper solicitation. Condition of NAIIA membership.

records.organization: National Association of Public Insurance Adjusters
records.notes: Public adjusters represent policyholders (not insurers). 10 rules: fairness, no misrepresentation, fee transparency, professional competency, no unauthorized law practice, conflict avoidance. Best interest duty to client.
Applies to RIMS-CRMP certification holders. Competent and ethical performance, disclosure of criminal convictions, no discrimination or harassment. Enforced by RIMS Certification Commission.
Applies to all IRM members globally. Integrity, fair and respectful treatment, observance of laws and regulatory requirements. Disciplinary procedures for non-compliance.

records.document_title: Standards of Best Practice, Conduct and Ethics (PRM Code)
records.notes: Required study and adherence for PRM certification. Cross-cultural code. 20 Continuing Risk Learning credits/year required to maintain designation. Ethics & Professional Standards Committee functions as ombudsman.

records.organization: Society of Corporate Compliance and Ethics
records.document_title: Code of Professional Ethics for Compliance and Ethics Professionals
records.notes: Adopted Aug 29 2007. Requires refusal to consent to misconduct, escalation, possible resignation if unresolved, and reporting when required by law. 19,000+ members in 100+ countries. Heavily used in financial services compliance.

Dec 2024 edition. Adopts IESBA Code plus ACCA-specific requirements. Five fundamental principles: integrity, objectivity, confidentiality, professional competence and due care, professional behavior. Disciplinary Committee enforcement.

records.organization: International Ethics Standards Board for Accountants
records.document_title: International Code of Ethics for Professional Accountants (2024 Handbook)
records.notes: Global baseline adopted by 180+ IFAC member bodies (ACCA, AICPA, CPA Australia, ICAEW, ICAS, etc.). Five fundamental principles. Overseen by Public Interest Oversight Board (PIOB). Aug 2024 edition. Applies to professional accountants in public practice and business.

records.profession_name: Financial Risk Manager (FRM) / Energy Risk Professional (ERP)
records.notes: Dual-listed: also at K64-015 (Financial Analysis). Applies to risk professionals in both financial analysis (Div 64) and auxiliary risk management roles (Div 66).

records.document_title: Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct
records.notes: Dual-listed: also at K64-005. CFA charterholders working as investment advisers (Div 66) are equally bound by this code as those in direct financial analysis (Div 64).

records.document_title: Code of Ethics and Standards of Practice (2026 edition)
records.notes: One of the oldest professional ethics codes (adopted 1913, continuously updated). 2026 edition includes anti-harassment provisions tied to protected class status. Mandatory ethics training every 3 years. Enforcement through local/state REALTOR® boards with complaint and arbitration system. Membership revocation for violations.

First adopted 1959 (first Canadian real estate ethics code). Based on moral integrity, competent service, and dedication to public welfare. Requires written disclosure of agency relationships and conflicts of interest. Binding on all CREA members as condition of membership.

Administered through state/territory Real Estate Institute affiliates. Underpins training programs, codes of conduct, and awards programs. As Australian FIABCI chapter, REIA also applies FIABCI International Code of Ethics. Requires acting in client's best interests, ethical/fair/honest dealing, and protection of public against fraud.

Global ethics framework for real estate professionals. All members must agree to respect the FIABCI Code upon joining. FIABCI is a member of the International Ethics Standards Coalition and signatory to UN Global Compact 10 Principles. Member country associations (including REIA, NAR, CREA) align with this framework.

Effective February 2022, replacing prior Rules of Conduct for Members, Rules of Conduct for Firms, and Global Ethical Principles. Principles: honesty, integrity, competence, service, respect, responsibility. Mandatory CPD for chartered status. Peer review and disciplinary proceedings for violations. Also applies to Section F (construction surveying).

Founded 1933; one of the oldest property management ethics codes. Covers fiduciary duty, loyalty to client, non-commingling of funds, prohibition on material misrepresentation of client assets. Enforced by Ethics and Discipline Committee; membership or designation revocation for violations.

Corporate-level code for firms holding AMO accreditation. Covers fiduciary duties, non-commingling of client funds, avoidance of conflicts of interest, prohibition on material rebates/gifts. Accreditation revocation or letter of censure for violations. Stringently enforced by IREM.

records.organization: National Association of Residential Property Managers
records.document_title: Code of Ethics and Standards of Professionalism
records.notes: Adopted 1994, amended multiple times. Covers duty to public, non-discrimination, fiduciary responsibility, confidentiality, fair housing compliance. Mandatory ethics course every 4 years. FTC (2014) required elimination of competition-limiting provisions.
