Organized around Canons including unbiased analysis, public protection, and non-detrimental conduct toward profession. Enforced through Peer Review Proceedings (Regulation No. 6). Designation revocation for violations. Updated May 2022; 2025 version also available.

records.document_title: Principles of Appraisal Practice and Code of Ethics
records.notes: All members must subscribe. Covers honesty, impartiality, competency over financial gain, confidentiality, conflict avoidance, and five-year record retention. Formal written complaint process. Covers real estate, personal property, business valuation, and machinery/equipment appraisers.

records.document_title: USPAP Ethics Rule (within Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice)
records.notes: USPAP Ethics Rule is legally required for all licensed/certified appraisers in all US states. Three sections: Conduct, Management, Confidentiality. Prohibits predetermined value opinions in exchange for compensation. 2024 edition expanded non-discrimination obligations. Enforcement via state licensing boards. Most legally enforceable ethics framework in real estate.

Requires honesty, professional conduct, transparent communication, honest advertising, and non-circumvention of industry standards. NAMB L.I.S.A. (Lending Integrity Seal of Approval) augments enforcement with continuing education, criminal background check, and ethics grievance review process.

National MBA has Code of Conduct; state affiliates maintain Canons of Ethics. Covers non-discrimination, candor and fairness, timely loan processing, integrity of loan submissions, and confidentiality. Principles enforced at state/local association level.

records.document_title: Code of Ethics and Standards of Practice
records.notes: Ethics course required as part of CCIM designation curriculum. For REALTOR® members, processed through NAR Code of Ethics system. Non-REALTORS® subject to direct CCIM discipline. Covers commercial real estate investment and brokerage professionals.

records.organization: Society of Industrial and Office Realtors
records.document_title: Code of Ethical Principles and Standards of Professional Practice
records.profession_name: Industrial and Office Real Estate Specialist
records.notes: Approved 1998, effective 1999. Substantially consistent with NAR Code but adapted for commercial real estate. Includes USPAP compliance for appraisal activities and IREM Code compliance for property management activities. Governed by SIOR Ethics and Arbitration Procedures Manual; designation revocation for violations.
Adopted 1983; adopted by all 50 US states + DC as basis for state bar rules. Previous model was 1969 Model Code.

records.document_title: SRA Code of Conduct for Solicitors, RELs and RFLs
records.notes: Part of SRA Standards and Regulations, in force November 2019. Separate Code of Conduct for Firms also exists.

records.document_title: BSB Handbook — Code of Conduct for Barristers
records.notes: 10 Core Duties for barristers. Enforced by the Bar Standards Board.
Collaboration of state/territory law societies. Adopted across Australian jurisdictions. Violation = unsatisfactory professional conduct or professional misconduct.

records.organization: Federation of Law Societies of Canada
records.notes: Adopted by all Canadian common law jurisdictions. Updated regularly by Standing Committee on Model Code. Current edition 2024.

records.document_title: International Principles on Conduct for the Legal Profession
records.notes: Adopted Warsaw 2011; updated 2018. 10 core principles providing framework for national codes globally.
Predecessor to 2011 International Principles. Originally adopted 1956, revised 1988. Retained as historical reference.

records.organization: American Institute of Certified Public Accountants
records.notes: Current codified version effective December 15, 2014. Used by all US state boards of accountancy as model.

records.organization: Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales
records.notes: 2025 edition in force from 1 July 2025. Five fundamental principles: integrity, objectivity, professional competence and due care, confidentiality, professional behaviour.
ACCA adopts IESBA Code + supplementary requirements. Current version effective December 2024.

records.organization: Institute of Chartered Accountants of Scotland
records.notes: Changes effective 1 January 2022, incorporating IESBA 2018 revisions. 2025 edition includes technology-related confidentiality changes.

records.organization: CPA Canada (Chartered Professional Accountants of Canada)
records.notes: Administered by provincial CPA bodies (CPA Ontario, CPABC, CPA Manitoba, etc.). Harmonised across Canada.

records.organization: International Ethics Standards Board for Accountants
records.document_title: International Code of Ethics for Professional Accountants (including International Independence Standards)
records.notes: Revised and restructured 2018 edition came into effect June 2019. Underpins ICAEW, ACCA, ICAS, and all CCAB member body codes. 2024/2025 handbook available.

records.document_title: Code of Ethics / Global Internal Audit Standards (Domain II — Ethics and Professionalism)
records.notes: 2024 Global Internal Audit Standards integrate ethics as Domain II. Applies to all IIA members, certification holders, and internal audit practitioners.
Adopted January 1, 2001. Also adopted by CAS, ASPPA, and Conference of Consulting Actuaries. Enforced by Actuarial Board for Counseling and Discipline (ABCD).
IAA membership requires member associations to have codes of conduct, discipline processes, and educational standards.
Applies to all IMC USA members and Certified Management Consultants (CMC). Ethics Committee enforces via Rules of Procedure.

records.organization: International Council of Management Consulting Institutes
records.document_title: ICMCI Core Code of Ethics (minimum guidelines)
records.notes: International umbrella body for national IMC institutes and globally recognised certifying body for CMCs.

records.document_title: Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct
records.notes: Updated version effective 17 November 2025. Four core values: responsibility, respect, fairness, honesty. Applies to all PMI members, volunteers, and certification holders.

records.document_title: Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct
records.notes: First published 2015 (50th Anniversary); recently revised. Mandatory for all acting on behalf of IPMA.

records.organization: Chartered Institute of Personnel and Development
records.notes: Effective 1 January 2023. Replaced 2012 Code. Covers HR, L&D, OD professionals.

records.organization: Chartered Institute of Procurement and Supply
records.notes: 64,000+ members in 180 countries. Breach may lead to disciplinary action under CIPS Royal Charter. Compliance required for Chartered Status.
First adopted 1914; major 2020 revision to stakeholder model (society, natural environment, profession, clients/employers, peers). First wholesale update since 1974.
Accompanied by 'Advice on Ethical Conduct' (2023 update). Applies to all ICE members globally.

records.organization: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers
records.notes: First established 1963; revised periodically. Applies to all IEEE members worldwide (~400,000 members in 160+ countries).
By-laws and Code of Conduct apply to all IMechE members. Aligns with UK Engineering Council UK-SPEC ethical principles.
2024 edition modernised to include cyber security, sustainability, D&I, social media. Compliance is condition of IChemE membership.
Canons first published 1946; current Code adopted 1964. Board of Ethical Review issues written opinions on ethical cases. Six fundamental canons.

records.document_title: Code of Ethics and Guidelines on Professional Conduct
records.notes: 2022 edition. Four core values: integrity, competence, leadership, sustainability.
Released at General Assembly 14 October 2023. Designed to assist member organisations in formulating their own codes. 90+ nation members.

records.document_title: Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct
records.notes: Current as of February 1, 2024. Three-tier structure: Canons, Ethical Standards, Rules of Conduct. Enforced by National Ethics Council.
Came into effect 1 May 2019 (revised 2018); supplementary guidance updated April 2021. Three principles: integrity, competence, relationships.

records.document_title: UIA Accord on Recommended International Standards of Professionalism in Architectural Practice — Policy on Ethics and Conduct
records.notes: Adopted Beijing June 1999; updated 2017. Intended as model code for UIA member sections.
Canon structure with Ethical Standards and mandatory Rules. ASLA also has a separate Code of Environmental Ethics.
Effective 2 February 2022. Applies globally to all RICS members and regulated firms. CPD requirement on ethics every 3 years. Previous version in place since 2007.
All FIDIC member associations subscribe to these principles. Promotes Quality-Based Selection (QBS) and anti-corruption stance.

records.document_title: Code of Ethics for the Professional Practice of Industrial Hygiene
records.notes: Provides standards for protecting health and well-being of working people. Board for Global EHS Credentialing (BGC) maintains an enforceable Code of Ethics.

records.document_title: The European Code of Conduct for Research Integrity (2023 Revised Edition)
records.notes: Published 23 June 2023. Recognised by European Commission as primary standard for Horizon-funded research. Increasingly serves as model for national codes globally. First edition 2011, revised 2017.

records.organization: World Conferences on Research Integrity Foundation
records.notes: Developed at 2nd World Conference on Research Integrity, Singapore, July 2010. 340 attendees from 51+ countries. 4 principles + 14 responsibilities. First international effort for unified research ethics policies.
Fosters values-based culture for ISC participants. Broader governance document for the world science community.

records.document_title: Declaration of Helsinki — Ethical Principles for Medical Research Involving Human Participants
records.notes: Originally adopted 1964; 8th revision adopted October 2024 (37 paragraphs). Cornerstone of human subjects research ethics globally.
Approved February 2011; replaced 1992 Ethical Standards. Nearly 3-year development process.

records.organization: International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry / Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons
records.document_title: Code of Ethical Principles of Chemistry
records.notes: Joint IUPAC-OPCW initiative. Focuses on dual-use chemistry and peaceful applications. Promotes ethics education in university chemistry curricula.
Voluntary principles emphasising truthfulness, substantiation, fair treatment, transparency, and privacy protection.
First adopted 1924. Prohibit false/misleading claims, offensive content, competitive disparagement. Unethical agencies denied membership.
Widely regarded as industry standard. No formal enforcement but membership may be restricted. Six core values + six code provisions of conduct.

records.document_title: ICCO Warsaw Principles — Ethical Use of AI in Public Relations and Communications
records.notes: Ratified at 2023 ICCO Global Summit in Warsaw. Represents 41 national PR associations across 82 countries, 3,000+ PR firms.

records.document_title: ICC/ESOMAR International Code on Market, Opinion and Social Research and Data Analytics
records.notes: Joint code since 1977. Mandatory for ESOMAR members; recognised by 60+ associations in 50+ countries. 2025 revision forthcoming.
In effect from 14 August 2023. Applies to all MRS members and Company Partners. Focuses on participant wellbeing, transparency, and inclusive data practices.

records.organization: AIGA — The Professional Association for Design
records.notes: Covers duties to clients, other designers, and society. Addresses fees, credit, conflicts of interest, and intellectual property.
Enforced by PPA Ethics Committee composed of PPA members.

records.document_title: Code of Ethics for Visual Journalists
records.notes: Emphasises truth, accuracy, and dignity. Prohibits staging photographs or manipulating news events.
Members agree to adhere as condition of membership. Emphasises professionalism, honesty, and respect for rights and dignity.

records.document_title: Code of Ethics and Professional Responsibility
records.notes: All ATA members must commit to CEPR. Sanctions list published. Covers honesty, competence, conflict of interest, confidentiality, accuracy.
Only global association of conference interpreters. Founded 1953; 3,000+ members in 100+ countries. Code revised 2022. Covers confidentiality, accuracy, dignity, working conditions, CPD.
Represents 80,000+ translators in 65 countries through 100+ associations. Code covers confidentiality, accuracy, integrity, and impartiality.

records.document_title: Principles of Veterinary Medical Ethics of the AVMA
records.notes: Three core principles: Stewardship, Integrity, Respect. Violation may result in AVMA disciplinary action. Most recent revision circulated 2024.

records.document_title: Code of Professional Conduct for Veterinary Surgeons
records.notes: Regulates under Veterinary Surgeons Act 1966. Statutory basis. Separate Code for Veterinary Nurses also exists. All vets take professional declaration on admission.
Aspirational/educational; state Veterinary Surgeons Boards hold regulatory enforcement authority. Four core values: professionalism, knowledge, community, adaptability.
Updated 2019 from 2012 original. Not legally binding unless enacted in national legislation. Sets common European veterinary ethical standards.
Updated 2025 to include stronger One Health, sustainability, and lifelong learning commitments. Used by national veterinary bodies worldwide as template for graduation oath.
Establishes industry principles for ethical conduct and professional service in equipment leasing/financing. Membership pledge required.

Very detailed code covering general conduct, consumer disclosure, resort management, resale activities, enforcement. PDF: https://www.arda.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/arda-code-of-ethics.pdf. Binding condition of membership. 300+ member companies.

records.document_title: SHRM Code of Ethical and Professional Standards in Human Resource Management
records.notes: One of the most influential HR ethics frameworks globally. First developed 1972. Six core principles: professional responsibility, professional development, ethical leadership, fairness and justice, conflicts of interest, use of information. SHRM-CP/SCP certification requires adherence.

records.organization: Chartered Institute of Personnel and Development
records.notes: Royal Charter body. Code effective Jan 2023, superseding prior Code of Professional Conduct. Applies to all CIPD, MCIPD, FCIPD members. Disciplinary cases published online at https://www.cipd.org/uk/membership/professional-standards/code-of-conduct/cases/. Active enforcement. PDF: https://www.cipd.org/globalassets/media/comms/code-of-conduct/2023-cipd-code-of-conduct-and-ethics.pdf

records.document_title: Code of Ethics and Rules of Professional Conduct
records.notes: Self-regulatory body under Ontario Human Resources Professionals Act, 2013. Code updated 2022. PDF: https://www.hrpa.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/HRPA-Code-of-Ethics-and-Rules-of-Professional-Conduct.pdf. Disciplinary process exists.

records.document_title: ASA Code of Ethics and Good Practices
records.notes: Three separate codes: general (https://americanstaffing.net/asa/asa-code-of-ethics/), search and placement (https://americanstaffing.net/asa/asa-code-of-ethics/search-and-placement-code-of-ethics/), day labor (https://americanstaffing.net/asa/asa-code-of-ethics/code-of-ethics-day-labor/). Membership pledge required.

records.document_title: NAPS Code of Ethics and Standards of Ethical Practices
records.notes: NAPS Accreditation (NAF) specifically requires Code of Ethics compliance. Standards of Ethical Practices at https://www.naps360.org/page/StandardsOfEthical. Binding for accredited member firms.

records.organization: Association of Executive Search and Leadership Consultants
records.document_title: Code of Professional Conduct and Professional Practice Standards
records.notes: Also at https://www.aesc.org/about-us/our-standards. Core values: ethics & integrity, excellence, objectivity, diversity & inclusion. Includes Client Bill of Rights and Candidate Bill of Rights. Regularly updated.
Core principles: accuracy, disclosure, consumer protection. All ASTA members pledge adherence as condition of membership. One of the oldest travel industry ethics frameworks.

Over 60 years old; regularly updated (Oct 2020 version). Covers advertising accuracy, fair trading terms, booking changes, complaint management. ABTA Code of Conduct Committee enforces; sanctions include membership suspension. Often cited as industry role model. PDF: https://www.abta.com/sites/default/files/2020-10/Code%20of%20Conduct%20Oct%202020.pdf

records.document_title: SITE Code of Ethics and Conduct
records.notes: 3,600+ members in 90 countries. Members agree to embrace SITE Creed and Code of Ethics. Complaint process outlined on site. Founded 1973.

CROSS-LISTING from Section H (Transportation, Division 51 - Air Transport). Relevant to Div. 79 for travel agency accreditation standards. PDF at https://www.iata.org/contentassets/c135b70ae5f34013b120b5008ca13369/code-business-conduct.pdf. Applies to all IATA employees and, as far as possible, consultants and partners.

Flagship global security management ethics document. Separate Code of Conduct at https://www.asisonline.org/security-news/code-of-ethics-and-code-of-conduct/code-of-conduct/. Certification Code of Professional Responsibility for CPP/PSP/PCI credential holders at https://www.asisonline.org/certification/professional-code-of-conduct/. Hub: https://www.asisonline.org/security-news/code-of-ethics-and-code-of-conduct/

records.document_title: CFE Code of Professional Standards / Code of Professional Ethics
records.notes: Five principles: integrity, objectivity, confidentiality, competency, professionalism. All ACFE members must agree to abide by Code. Separate Rules of Conduct with formal disciplinary procedures. Credential revocation possible. CFE Code of Professional Standards PDF: https://www.acfe.com/about-the-acfe/-/media/E805D87A1E144558BF27A7F4B0B8317B.ashx

records.organization: National Council of Investigation and Security Services
records.document_title: NCISS Code of Ethics and Professional Standards
records.notes: 2021 version at https://www.nciss.org/code-of-ethics-2021. Covers competency, confidentiality, conflict of interest, truth in advertising, employee standards. Binding for member firms.

records.document_title: Code of Ethics (adopting Hailey Code of Professional Conduct)
records.notes: In 2023 NALI adopted 'Code of Professional Conduct: Standards and Ethics for the Investigative Profession, 4th ed.' by Kitty Hailey as its governing standard. Focused on attorney-directed legal investigation. CLI credential linked.

records.organization: National Association of Professional Process Servers
records.notes: Requires all work be performed in a lawful, professional and ethical manner. Prohibits conduct impugning the Association's reputation. Membership binding.
Required for all IFMA members. Covers professional integrity, client service, conflict of interest. CFM (Certified Facility Manager) credential linked. International membership base.

Long-established; ethics history traces to early 20th century (https://www.asla.org/resources/library/archives-blog/ethics-history). Also has separate Code of Environmental Ethics: https://www.asla.org/about/ethics-and-professional-conduct/asla-code-of-environmental-ethics. Alt URL: https://www.asla.org/ContentDetail.aspx?id=4276

records.document_title: ASID Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct
records.notes: All ASID members agree to abide by code. PDF: https://www.asid.org/lib24watch/files/download/11528/72acfb02e2b83e8325fda91203f24b1c90213ebf. NCIDQ exam linked. Interior design has dual ISIC placement: Div. 74 (M-Professional) and Div. 81 (building services). Primary placement here as building/space services.

Covers administrative and office support professionals. Core values-based code. CAP (Certified Administrative Professional) credential references code. Historical 'Code of Ethics' also referenced in older materials.
Revised 2013; 8 core principles; Ethics and Standards Implementation Committee established 2014; complaints process for members only

records.organization: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
records.document_title: Recommendation of the Council on Public Integrity
records.notes: Three pillars: System, Culture, Accountability. OECD member government implementation

records.organization: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
records.document_title: Guidelines for Managing Conflict of Interest in the Public Service
records.notes: Central government level conflict of interest management for public officials

records.document_title: Standards of Conduct for the International Civil Service / UN Staff Regulations and Rules
records.notes: Governs all UN Secretariat staff; backed by ST/SGB/2018/1; core values: integrity, professionalism, respect for diversity

records.document_title: Tax Administration 2024 — Integrity and Organisational Culture Framework
records.notes: ISORA survey-based; includes data ethics framework; 50+ economies represented

records.organization: International Association of Chiefs of Police
records.notes: Originally adopted 1957; updated 2024; widely adopted as standard by US and international agencies; centerpiece of training programs

records.organization: International Association of Chiefs of Police
records.notes: Practical implementation resource for departments; supplements Code of Ethics

records.document_title: Code of Ethics for INTERPOL Officials (October 2023)
records.notes: Governs all INTERPOL General Secretariat staff; values: respect, integrity, excellence, teamwork, innovation

records.document_title: Code of Conduct for Members of the Armed Forces of the United States
records.notes: Established by EO 10631 (1955), amended 1988 (AR 350-30); enforced under Uniform Code of Military Justice

records.document_title: Army Values / Army Ethic White Paper
records.notes: 7 Army Values: LDRSHIP (Loyalty, Duty, Respect, Selfless Service, Honor, Integrity, Personal Courage); embedded in AR 600-100

records.document_title: DoD Directive 5500.07 — Ethics and Standards of Conduct
records.notes: Mandatory for all DoD employees, civilian and military; Standards of Conduct Office oversight

records.organization: International Committee of the Red Cross / State Parties to Geneva Conventions
records.document_title: Law of Armed Conflict / International Humanitarian Law
records.notes: Geneva Conventions 1949 + Additional Protocols; ICRC as guardian; binding international treaty law for 196 states
Last amended 2010; adopted/adapted by most US states; enforced by state judicial conduct commissions; original canons from 1924

records.organization: UN Office on Drugs and Crime / Judicial Group on Strengthening Judicial Integrity
records.notes: Six values: independence, impartiality, integrity, propriety, equality, competence and diligence; endorsed by UN ECOSOC Resolution 2006/23

records.document_title: Basic Principles on the Independence of the Judiciary (1985)
records.notes: Adopted by 7th UN Congress on Crime Prevention; endorsed by UNGA resolutions 40/32 and 40/146; addresses independence, tenure, secrecy, discipline
Governing instrument for all ICC judges; references Bangalore Principles and UN 1985 Basic Principles

records.document_title: Standards of Professional Responsibility and Statement of the Essential Duties and Rights of Prosecutors (1999, updated 2018)
records.notes: Adopted 1999; adopted by UN Commission on Crime Prevention (UNCCPCJ) 2008; covers professional conduct, disclosure, independence, impartiality
National standards summarizing best practices; voluntary adoption by DA offices; NDAA founded 1950

records.document_title: Foreign Affairs Manual (FAM) — Standards of Conduct
records.notes: Primary governance document for US Foreign Service; binding on Foreign Service and Civil Service personnel; regularly updated

records.document_title: Electoral Integrity Assessment / Electoral Leadership Ethics Training
records.notes: IFES since 1987; works with electoral management bodies in 145+ countries; Technical Election Assessment Mission methodology

records.organization: US Congress / Office of Government Ethics
records.document_title: Code of Ethics for Government Service (H.Con.Res.175, 1958)
records.notes: Congressional resolution 1958; 10 principles for all federal employees; incorporated into 5 CFR Part 2635 Standards of Ethical Conduct
Original 1975 code; updated version. NEA is the largest teacher union in the US with ~3 million members. Two principles: Commitment to the Student, Commitment to the Profession.
Adopted October 2018 by AFT Executive Council; revised July 2023. AFT has ~1.7 million members. Separate from the MCEE which AFT co-developed with NEA.
Founded 1994. Four principles: Students and Learning, Professional Practice, Colleagues, Community and Parents. Independent non-union alternative to NEA/AFT.

records.organization: National Association of State Directors of Teacher Education and Certification
records.document_title: Model Code of Ethics for Educators (MCEE), 2nd Edition
records.notes: First edition 2015; 2nd edition June 2023. Multi-stakeholder consensus code developed with NEA, AFT, NASSP, NAESP, CCSSO, and AACTE. Five principles, 18 sections, 86 standards. Widely adopted by states as basis for teacher licensure ethics requirements.
Formed 2017 by merger of NUT (National Union of Teachers, 1870) and ATL (Association of Teachers and Lecturers). Code embedded in union rules Appendix A. ~450,000 members.

records.document_title: International Code of Ethics for Educators
records.notes: Released October 5, 2018. Education International is the global federation representing ~400 education unions in 170 countries (~32 million members). Covers professional values, student relationships, societal responsibility, and digital ethics.

records.organization: National Association for the Education of Young Children
records.document_title: Code of Ethics for Early Childhood Educators
records.notes: First adopted 1989; revised 2005, 2011; draft revision 2024. Covers birth through age 8. Addresses responsibilities to children, families, colleagues, employers, communities, and society. Accompanied by Statement of Commitment. Widely used in ECE preparation programs.

records.document_title: CEC Ethical Principles and Practice Standards
records.notes: CEC is the primary professional organization for special education worldwide. Ethical principles include: maintaining challenging expectations, promoting participation, using evidence-based practice, protecting safety, and practicing within professional ethics. Covers initial and advanced preparation standards.

records.organization: National Association of Elementary School Principals
records.document_title: Statement of Ethics for School Administrators
records.notes: Shared statement with NASSP (both co-authored as school administrator ethics). Recently updated 2023. Emphasizes student well-being as primary priority, transcending political and personal biases.

records.organization: National Association of Secondary School Principals
records.notes: Reflects Mission Statement, Strategic Objectives, Statement of Ethics for School Administrators, and Policy Statements. Together with NAESP, NASSP co-authored the Professional Standards for Educational Leaders (PSEL 2015) through the National Policy Board for Educational Administration.

Originally adopted 1966; revised 1987 and 2009. Addresses responsibilities to subject/scholarship, students, colleagues, institution, and community. Foundational document for academic professional ethics in the US.

records.document_title: ASCA Ethical Standards for School Counselors
records.notes: Updated 2022 in consultation with state associations, counselor educators, and practitioners nationwide. Addresses responsibilities to students, parents, school, community, and self. Covers confidentiality, technology use, cultural competence, and dual relationships.

Effective July 1, 2020. Part of NASP 2020 Professional Standards (four components: practice, graduate preparation, credentialing, ethics). Members and NCSP certification holders are bound to comply. Four sections: Dignity and Rights, Professional Competence and Responsibility, Honesty and Integrity, Responsibility to Schools/Families/Society.

records.document_title: Code of Ethics of the American Library Association
records.notes: Most recent amendment 2021 added ninth principle on racial and social justice. Nine core principles covering intellectual freedom, privacy, confidentiality, service equity, honesty in information provision, and professional development. Used by librarians, library staff, and information professionals.

records.organization: Chartered Institute of Library and Information Professionals
records.document_title: CILIP Ethical Principles and Code of Professional Practice
records.notes: All members sign up to CILIP's ethical principles and code on joining. Royal Chartered body for library and information professionals. Ethics Committee provides guidance and periodic reviews. Covers human rights, equality and diversity, professional conduct, stewardship, confidentiality, and professional development.

records.organization: International Federation of Library Associations and Institutions
records.document_title: IFLA Code of Ethics for Librarians and other Information Workers
records.notes: Endorsed by IFLA Governing Board August 2012. Draws on national codes from 60+ countries. Short and full versions available. Covers access to information, privacy, transparency, professional conduct, equality, and knowledge economy. Over 1,400 member organizations in 140 countries.

records.document_title: SAA Core Values Statement and Code of Ethics for Archivists
records.notes: Significant revision approved August 2020. Original code introduced in 1980. Jointly used with Core Values of Archivists. Covers collection policies, preservation, access, privacy, donor relations, and professional relationships.

ARMA International is the professional association for records and information management (RIM). Code addresses three areas: society, employers, and the profession. Key principles include supporting free flow of information, maintaining accuracy, confidentiality, avoiding conflicts of interest.
Current edition with 9 Principles + Council Opinions. First promulgated 1847; continuously updated. Widely adopted by state medical boards though not legally binding.

records.document_title: WMA International Code of Medical Ethics
records.notes: 2022 major revision (4-year process); first adopted 1949. Adds provisions on environmental health, remote care, physician well-being.

records.document_title: WMA Declaration of Geneva — Physician's Pledge
records.notes: Modern Hippocratic Oath; first adopted 1948. 2017 revision was the largest update in decades, adding patient autonomy, physician self-care, medical knowledge sharing.

records.document_title: CMA Code of Ethics and Professionalism
records.notes: Updated 2018; one of profession's most important documents since 1868. Based on compassion, beneficence, non-maleficence, respect for persons, justice, accountability.
Effective January 30, 2024. Statutory regulator. Covers doctors, physician associates, and anaesthesia associates. 11 categories of professional standards.
Updated February 2025. Practical guidance (not rules) for ethical decision-making. Covers confidentiality, consent, children, mental capacity. Complementary to GMC standards.

records.document_title: Declaration of Professional Responsibility: Medicine's Social Contract with Humanity
records.notes: Adopted December 4, 2001. 9 duties transcending specialties. Drafted partly in response to September 11; addresses medicine's role in public health and global responsibilities.

records.document_title: Statement on Principles (Code of Professional Conduct)
records.notes: Originally 1913 (anti-fee-splitting focus); revised 1974, 2004, 2016. Covers Code of Professional Conduct, qualifications, surgeon-patient relationship, discrimination prohibition.

records.organization: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists
records.notes: Foundational principle: welfare of patient forms basis of all medical judgments. Multiple committee opinions supplement the core ethics code.

records.document_title: Code of Ethics for Nurses with Interpretive Statements
records.notes: Released January 29, 2025. 10 provisions (new 10th provision on global ethical issues added). Previous version was 2015. Nursing's ethical standard of practice and social contract.

records.document_title: ICN Code of Ethics for Nurses
records.notes: First adopted 1953; revised 2021 reflecting COVID-19 lessons. 4-element structure: nurses & people, nurses & practice, nurses & coworkers, nurses & profession.

records.document_title: The Code: Professional Standards of Practice and Behaviour for Nurses, Midwives and Nursing Associates
records.notes: October 2018 version current. Required for UK registration. 4 themes: prioritise people, practise effectively, preserve safety, promote professionalism and trust.

records.document_title: Code of Members' Professional Values and Behaviour
records.notes: Applies to all RCN members. Complementary to NMC Code. Emphasizes maintaining professional reputation, respect, confidentiality.

records.organization: National Association of Directors of Nursing Administration in Long Term Care
records.notes: Covers nursing administration in LTC settings. Supports quality of care for individuals receiving and delivering long-term care.

records.document_title: Principles of Ethics and Code of Professional Conduct
records.notes: March 2023 version current. Three-part structure: Principles of Ethics (aspirational), Code of Professional Conduct (binding), Advisory Opinions. 5 fundamental principles: autonomy, nonmaleficence, beneficence, justice, veracity.
Effective September 30, 2013. 9 principles for all dental team members. Failure may result in fitness to practise proceedings and removal from GDC Register.
Adopted October 2024. Specific to dental hygienists.
Established 1852; most recent revision 1994. 8 principles based on moral obligations and virtues. Covers covenantal relationship, compassion, autonomy, justice.

records.document_title: Statement of Professional Standards: Codes of Ethics for Pharmacists
records.notes: FIP Council approved 2014. Adopted by professional organizations in 91 countries. Oath/promise available in 18 languages. Covers autonomy, beneficence, non-maleficence, justice.
9 standards applicable in all practice settings. UK statutory regulator for pharmacists and pharmacy technicians in Great Britain. Updated patient safety standards April 2024.

records.document_title: Professional Standards for Hospital Pharmacy Services
records.notes: First published 2012; 2017 version current. Covers acute, mental health, private, community, hospice, ambulance settings. Multiple domain-specific professional standards documents.

records.document_title: Code of Ethics for the Physical Therapist
records.notes: 2020 version current. July 2025 APTA House of Delegates adopted new unified Code of Ethics for Physical Therapy Profession (combining PT and PTA standards), effective January 1, 2026.
Formerly WCPT; in official relations with WHO since 1952. Represents 600,000+ physiotherapists through 129 member organizations. Ethical Principles define professional duties globally.

records.document_title: Code of Members' Professional Values and Behaviour
records.notes: 2019 revision. 4 core principles: taking responsibility for actions, behaving ethically, delivering effective service, striving for excellence. Applies to all roles and career stages.

records.document_title: Standards of Conduct, Performance and Ethics
records.notes: Effective September 1, 2024. UK statutory regulator for 15+ allied health professions including physiotherapists, OTs, radiographers, speech therapists, dietitians, paramedics, psychologists. 7 core standards.
2025 edition (previous was 2020). 7 core values + 6 guiding principles: beneficence, non-maleficence, autonomy, justice, veracity, fidelity. First formal code established 1975.

records.document_title: WFOT Guiding Principles for Ethical Occupational Therapy
records.notes: 2024 update (replaced 2016 Code of Ethics). 101 national OT organizations represented. Endorses UN Universal Declaration of Human Rights. Serves as guide for member associations.
First established 1952; regularly updated. Covers Certificate of Clinical Competence holders and members. Requires 1 CEU ethics hour per 3-year certification cycle.

records.organization: Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics / Commission on Dietetic Registration
records.document_title: Code of Ethics for the Nutrition and Dietetics Profession
records.profession_name: Registered Dietitian Nutritionist/Nutrition and Dietetic Technician
records.notes: Effective June 1, 2018. Joint Academy/CDR document. Reviewed codes of 11 professional associations. 4 moral principles: non-maleficence, autonomy, beneficence, justice.

records.organization: American Society of Radiologic Technologists / American Registry of Radiologic Technologists
records.document_title: Code of Ethics / Standards of Ethics
records.notes: Joint ASRT/ARRT ethical framework. ARRT Standards of Ethics 2020. Covers competence, patient care, confidentiality, non-discrimination, continuing education.

records.document_title: Statement of Ethics and Professional Conduct
records.notes: AARC position statement. Defines basic ethical and moral standards. Covers integrity, competence, patient rights, privacy, non-discrimination, anti-fraud provisions.

records.document_title: Ethical Principles of Psychologists and Code of Conduct
records.notes: 2002 code; 2010 and 2017 amendments. 5 General Principles (aspirational) + enforceable Ethical Standards. Widely adopted by state licensing boards. Draft 2024/2025 revision in progress.

records.document_title: The Principles of Medical Ethics with Annotations Especially Applicable to Psychiatry
records.notes: Annotates AMA Principles with psychiatric-specific guidance. First psychiatric-specific ethics code adopted 1970 in response to public concerns. Covers confidentiality, boundary violations, informed consent. Includes Goldwater Rule.
2014 revision. Expanded guidance on technology, social media, distance counseling, multicultural considerations. 6 fundamental ethical principles. Widely used across counseling specialties.
Approved May 2023, revised August 2023. 114 ethical standards in 6 areas including telemental health, social media, technology. Largest national counselor credentialing body.

records.organization: American Association for Marriage and Family Therapy
records.notes: Revised AAMFT Code of Ethics effective January 1, 2026. Core values include equity, belonging, mutual respect, diversity. Enforced by AAMFT Ethics Committee.

records.organization: International Association of Marriage and Family Counselors
records.notes: Adopted 2017; published 2018. Division of the American Counseling Association. 10 sections covering all aspects of couple and family counseling including multicultural inclusion.

records.organization: NAADAC — The Association for Addiction Professionals / National Certification Commission for Addiction Professionals
records.notes: 2021 update (previous revision 2016). Covers full continuum: prevention, intervention, treatment, recovery support. Required by many state certification boards. Guiding values: fidelity, loyalty, diligence, discretion, non-maleficence.

records.organization: National Association of Emergency Medical Technicians
records.notes: Originally drafted by Charles Gillespie MD in 1978; first revised June 14, 2013. 6 core principles: professionalism, respect, integrity, compassion, accountability, excellence. Patient-centered update.

records.document_title: Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct
records.notes: Three-document suite: Code of Ethics, Optometric Oath, Standards of Professional Conduct (adopted June 2011). Standards organized under 4 bioethical principles (autonomy, non-maleficence, beneficence, justice).

records.document_title: Standards of Practice for Optometrists and Dispensing Opticians
records.notes: 19 standards of behaviour. UK statutory regulator for optical professions. College of Optometrists provides supplementary Guidance for Professional Practice (2023 edition).
Based on primary responsibility to benefit the patient. Addresses excellence, professional conduct, sexual misconduct prohibition, anti-abandonment, healthcare collaboration.
2017 version. APMA members obligated to follow as part of membership. Addresses patient safety supervision, conflict of interest, gifts/gratuities, fraud prevention.

records.document_title: Code of Ethics with Explanatory Statements
records.notes: Foundation document for midwifery practice in US. Emphasizes human rights, dignity, autonomy, justice. Covers practice, research, education responsibilities. AMCB references ACNM code for discipline.

records.document_title: International Code of Ethics for Midwives
records.notes: Established 1993; revised and re-confirmed 1999 at ICM Council in Manila. 4 sections: midwifery relationships, practice, professional responsibilities, advancement of knowledge.

Effective November 2019; replaced 2002 code. Not disciplinary; provides ethical framework. Emphasizes social justice, equity, community health. First national public health ethics code was APHA's 2002 adoption.

records.document_title: WHO Global Code of Practice on the International Recruitment of Health Personnel
records.notes: Adopted at 63rd World Health Assembly 2010; reviewed 2023. Ethical principles for international health personnel recruitment. Aims to protect health systems of developing countries.

Amended by Board of Governors November 13, 2017. Adherence is a membership requirement. Covers relationships with colleagues, patients, organization, community, society. 3 fundamental objectives of healthcare leadership profession.

records.document_title: Shared Code of Conduct for Registered Health Practitioners
records.notes: Shared by 12 of 15 National Boards. Medical, Nursing/Midwifery, Psychology Boards have profession-specific codes. Defines expected professional behaviour for registered health practitioners.

records.organization: National Association of Directors of Nursing Administration in Long Term Care
records.notes: Covers nursing administration in long-term care residential settings. Promotes quality of care for individuals receiving and delivering long-term care.

records.document_title: Code of Ethics and Standards of Practice for Aging Life Care Professionals
records.profession_name: Aging Life Care Professional/Geriatric Care Manager
records.notes: Originally 1990 (as NAPGCM); name changed 2015; most recent revision June 2025. Professional Conduct Review Committee enforces. Covers geriatric care management in residential/home settings.

records.organization: National Association for Home Care & Hospice
records.notes: Adopted September 1982 by NAHC Board of Directors. 8 sections: patient rights, agency-patient relationships, inter-agency cooperation, referrals, staffing, ethical financial practices, marketing, community service. Ethics Committee handles breaches.

records.organization: American Association on Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities
records.notes: First adopted 2012 by Board of Directors; revised January 29, 2020. Covers professionals serving individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities in residential and community settings.
First approved 1960; 2021 revision adds professional self-care, updates cultural competence standard. 150+ specific guidelines across 6 areas. Most widely used US social work ethics code.

records.organization: International Federation of Social Workers / International Association of Schools of Social Work
records.document_title: Global Social Work Statement of Ethical Principles
records.notes: Approved at General Meetings in Dublin, July 2018. Replaces 2004 Ethics in Social Work Statement of Principles. Covers digital technology ethics, human rights, social justice. National associations develop specific codes from this framework.

records.document_title: Code of Ethics for Social Work
records.notes: In place since 1975; 2021 refreshed version. Binding on all BASW members in all roles across UK. Emphasizes human rights, social justice, professional integrity, anti-oppressive practice.
November 2020 revision. 3 core values (simplified from previous edition). Part of regulatory suite with Australian Social Work Education and Accreditation Standards.

records.document_title: Code of Ethics, Values and Guiding Principles
records.notes: Released January 8, 2024. 7 values incorporating Truth and Reconciliation principles and Indigenous rights (new). Developed with input from ~2,000 members.

records.document_title: Ethical Standards for Human Service Professionals
records.notes: 2024 revision; previous version 2015. 44 standards in 7 areas: clients, colleagues, profession, public/society, employers, self, students. Addresses technology, telehealth, social media additions.

records.document_title: Code of Preferred Practices / Creative Rights Handbook (2023–2026)
records.notes: Rights and preferred practices backed by DGA Basic Agreement with studios; includes creative control provisions; updated 2023-2026

records.document_title: WGA Community Standards (professional conduct and anti-harassment)
records.notes: Focuses on harassment, power dynamics, and professional conduct in writers rooms; WGA also has WGAE (East) parallel structure

records.document_title: Code of Conduct on Discrimination and Harassment
records.notes: Addresses discrimination, harassment, professional integrity; complaints process available; AFM has 70,000+ members in US and Canada
Historical code governing professional conduct between musicians; AFM's foundational ethics reference
Founded London 1921; pledge to oppose censorship and suppression of free expression; 144 PEN centres worldwide; Writers in Prison Committee monitors 900+ cases annually
9 core principles (9th added 2021 — racial and social justice); broadly adopted as policy standard by library employers; intellectual freedom, privacy, equitable service

records.organization: International Federation of Library Associations and Institutions
records.document_title: Code of Ethics for Librarians and other Information Workers (2012)
records.notes: Endorsed by IFLA Governing Board August 2012; model drawing on 60+ national codes; covers access, neutrality, privacy, open access, professional excellence

records.organization: Chartered Institute of Library and Information Professionals
records.document_title: Ethical Principles and Code of Professional Practice
records.notes: All CILIP members must agree upon joining; chartered professional body; regular ethics review process; addresses human rights, public benefit, confidentiality

records.document_title: Core Values Statement and Code of Ethics (revised 2020)
records.notes: Council approved revision August 2020; addresses access, privacy, authenticity, professional relationships, accountability; ethics committee oversight
Adopted Beijing September 6, 1996; available in 24 languages; covers integrity, access, privacy, professional cooperation; adopted by national archival associations worldwide

records.document_title: ICOM Code of Ethics for Museums (adopted 1986, revised 2004; 2024 revision in progress)
records.notes: Adopted 1986; major revision 2004; 2024 revision process underway; mandatory for ICOM member institutions; translated into 38 languages; covers acquisition, deaccessioning, repatriation, security
Required for AAM museum accreditation; institutional code + individual professional duties; loyalty to mission as core principle

records.document_title: Code of Ethics for Art Museum Directors / Professional Practices in Art Museums
records.notes: First published 1971; major revision 2011; prohibits personal dealing in artworks; sanctions include membership suspension; Professional Practices document revised at 10-year intervals

records.organization: American Alliance of Museums — Collections Professionals
records.document_title: Code of Ethics and Professional Practices for Collections Professionals (2021)
records.notes: Fiduciary duty of care framework; covers stewardship, legal compliance, conflict of interest

records.organization: Association of Registrars and Collections Specialists
records.notes: Specialized code for registrars and collections managers; supplements AAM code

records.document_title: Responsible Gaming Code of Conduct (Member Code of Conduct)
records.notes: Covers responsible gaming, underage gambling prevention, alcohol service, advertising standards; AGA members invest hundreds of millions annually in responsible gaming; founded 1994

records.document_title: Licence Conditions and Codes of Practice (LCCP) — Social Responsibility Code
records.notes: Mandatory for all UK gambling licensees; LCCP SR Code 3.4.1 requires customer interaction to minimize gambling harm; fines and licence revocation for violations

records.document_title: Internet Responsible Gaming Standards / Responsible Gambling Principles
records.notes: NCPG founded 1972; iCAP compliance assessment program; responsible sports gambling principles; standards for treatment providers and operators
IOC first established independent Ethics Commission 1999; code covers conflict of interest, competition manipulation, gifts; 9-member Ethics Commission; sanctions including expulsion

records.profession_name: Football Official / Referee / Player / Coach / Agent
records.notes: FIFA Ethics Committee established 2006 (post-referee bribery scandal); independent investigatory and adjudicatory chambers; fines min CHF 100,000 + bans up to 3 years for betting violations

records.document_title: WADA Code of Ethics (adopted 2021, revised November 2023) + World Anti-Doping Code (2021)
records.notes: WADA founded 1999; Code adopted by 650+ sports organizations; WA Anti-Doping Code first 2003, current version 2021; WADA Code of Ethics governs WADA officials specifically

5 parts: introduction, definitions, core values (4: Professionalism, Collaboration, Humanity, Equity), ethical standards (28), professional pledge; credential revocation for violations; previous version 2020

records.document_title: NSCA Codes, Policies, and Procedures (incl. Code of Ethics)
records.notes: Replaces earlier separate Code of Ethics; Ethics Committee oversight; anti-discrimination, dignity, confidentiality; award revocation for violations

records.document_title: Code of Ethics and Conduct for ACE Certified Professionals
records.notes: Required for ACE certification; covers safe instruction, equal treatment, CPR/AED currency, confidentiality, professional boundaries, scope of practice, referral obligations
Covers evidence-based practice, confidentiality, scope of practice, scientific integrity, anti-misconduct; censure and membership loss for violations

records.document_title: CPRP Code of Conduct (Certified Park and Recreation Professional)
records.notes: Required for CPRP credential; governs recreation professionals in public parks agencies; profession has specialized training, credentials, and ethics requirements

records.document_title: ASAE Standards of Conduct / Code of Conduct
records.notes: Core Ethical Standards cover: basic conduct, confidentiality, competition, giving and receiving. ASAE is the meta-level governance body for association executives. Ethics Toolkit (2025): https://www.asaecenter.org/-/media/models-and-samples/6/6/1/5/ASAE-Ethics-Toolkit-March-2025.ashx. Standards PDF: https://www.asaecenter.org/-/media/ASAE/Files/AboutASAE/Standards-Of-Conduct-SEPT-23-2022.ashx

records.organization: American Federation of Labor and Congress of Industrial Organizations
records.notes: Applicable to all AFL-CIO workplaces, events, activities, meetings. Covers anti-discrimination, anti-harassment, professional conduct. PDF: https://aflcio.org/sites/default/files/2018-02/AFL-CIO%20Code%20of%20Conduct%20-%20Final.pdf. AFL-CIO Constitution (Article X) also requires affiliated unions to adopt own ethical practices codes. Represents 12.5 million members.

All CompTIA-certified persons must agree to this code. Covers: no dishonesty/fraud/deceit; no unauthorized IT system breach; no cheating. A+ and other CompTIA certs are common in Div. 95 repair roles. CROSS-LISTING: also appears in J62 (ICT) for cybersecurity context.

Membership prerequisite. Two tiers: Principles of Ethics (aspirational) and Rules of Ethics (mandatory). Covers client welfare, professional conduct, confidentiality, scope of practice. PDF: https://tn.wp.amtamassage.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/50/2011/03/code_of_ethics_AMTA.pdf

records.document_title: ABMP Code of Ethics for Massage Therapists
records.notes: Second major US massage therapy membership organization. Code covers client dignity, confidentiality, professional boundaries, scope of practice. Membership binding. Parallel to AMTA code.
Covers client confidentiality, scope of practice, professional conduct, honest representation of qualifications, legal compliance. NCEA Certified (NC) credential linked.

PBA absorbed the National Cosmetology Association (NCA). Separate codes for manufacturers, distributors, salon/spa owners, licensed professionals (pledge at probeauty.org/pledge). Covers health/safety standards, professionalism, ethical behavior. NCA heritage incorporated.

CROSS-LISTING: also classifiable under G47 (Retail, mortuary goods). Code covers obligations to: the family, care of decedent, public, government, NFDA members. PDF: https://nfda.org/Portals/0/NFDAORG/About/Professional_Conduct/Code-of-Professional-Conduct.pdf. Approved October 19, 2002.

Sets values, principles, and standards for Certified Matchmakers. Core values: customer service, dignity of person, importance of human relationships, integrity, competence. Covers responsibilities to clients, colleagues, practice settings, and the profession. Addresses client self-determination.

records.document_title: Code of Conduct for Au Pair Organisations
records.notes: NOTE: This code governs au pair PLACEMENT AGENCIES (Division 78 — Employment Activities), NOT individual household employers (Division 97). Included here as the closest normative instrument touching the Div. 97 household-employer ecosystem. Sets standards for selection of au pairs and families, ethical treatment, professional conduct. ISIC primary classification: Division 78.
records.isic_classification_note: Properly classified: Division 78 (Employment Activities). Cross-listed here for Div. 97 household employment context.

records.notes: International treaty framework establishing minimum labor standards for domestic workers: rest periods, minimum wage, protection from abuse, minimum age. Adopted June 16, 2011; entered into force September 5, 2013. This is a REGULATORY/TREATY FRAMEWORK, not a professional association ethics code. Included as the best available normative framework for Div. 97. Full text also at https://www.un.org/en/development/desa/population/migration/generalassembly/docs/globalcompact/ILO_C_189.pdf
records.document_type_note: Treaty/convention — not a professional association code of ethics. No professional body equivalent found for household employers.

records.document_title: Standards of Conduct for the International Civil Service / UN Ethics Framework
records.notes: UN Ethics Office established 2006. Five functions: advice; retaliation protection; financial disclosure; ethics training; standards coherence. Core values: integrity, professionalism, respect for diversity. ICSC Standards of Conduct govern all UN system staff. CROSS-LISTING from O84 (International Affairs/Public Administration). Policy portal: https://policy.un.org/en/accountability/ethical-standards-and-integrity

Standalone Code of Ethics (June 2020) separate from general UN framework. PDF: https://www.undp.org/sites/g/files/zskgke326/files/undp/library/corporate/ethics/UNDP%20CODE%20OF%20ETHICS%20-%20June%202020.pdf. Ethics Office: advice, retaliation protection, training, financial disclosure. POPP portal: https://popp.undp.org/accountability/ethics

records.document_title: IMF Code of Conduct for Staff
records.profession_name: IMF Staff / International Financial Institution Employee
records.notes: Covers all IMF employees. Separate Executive Board Code of Conduct at https://www.imf.org/external/hrd/edscode.htm. Ethical Conduct and Core Values Certification policy: https://www.imf.org/en/About/ethics-and-integrity/ethical-conduct-and-core-values-certification-and-financial-disclosure-policy-for-imf-staff. Annual ethics and integrity reports published publicly. Staff financial disclosure required.

records.document_title: World Bank Group Code of Ethics
records.profession_name: World Bank Group Staff / Development Finance Professional
records.notes: Core values: impact, integrity, respect, teamwork, innovation. PDF: https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/147281468337279671/pdf/WBG-Code-of-Ethics.pdf. Separate Board Officials Code of Conduct. INT (Integrity Vice Presidency) enforces. Whistleblower protections. Sanctions regime for misconduct.

Agreed by North Atlantic Council December 18, 2020. Applies to all NATO civilian and military staff across all NATO bodies. Core principles: integrity, loyalty, accountability, impartiality, professionalism. Read alongside NATO Civilian Personnel Regulations.

records.document_title: Code of Conduct for Members of the European Commission
records.notes: Updated 2018; covers all Commissioners during and after tenure (post-service restrictions, cooling-off periods). EC Staff ethics: https://commission.europa.eu/about/service-standards-and-principles/ethics-and-good-administration/staff-and-ethics_en. European Ombudsman oversees EU ethics: https://www.ombudsman.europa.eu/webpub/2024/ethics-standards/en/. Independent Ethical Committee enforces.

records.organization: International Committee of the Red Cross
records.document_title: Code of Conduct for Employees of the ICRC
records.notes: Covers internal ethical obligations of ICRC staff (integrity, accountability, humanitarian principles). PDF (2023): https://www.icrc.org/en/download/file/271318/code_of_conduct_2023.pdf. SEPARATE from the humanitarian sector-wide Code of Conduct for the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement and NGOs in Disaster Relief (IFRC, 1992): https://www.ifrc.org/document/code-conduct-international-red-cross-and-red-crescent-movement-and-ngos-disaster-relief. CROSS-LISTING from O84.

records.organization: Red Cross / Red Crescent Movement and NGOs
records.document_title: Code of Conduct for the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement and NGOs in Disaster Relief
records.notes: Drawn up 1992 by Steering Committee for Humanitarian Response (SCHR). Sets industry-wide ethical standards for humanitarian operations. Signed by major international humanitarian organizations. Foundational humanitarian sector ethics code. Distinct from the ICRC employee code (ISIC-U99-007) above.

records.document_title: UNESCO Ethics Office Handbook for Ethical Conduct
records.notes: UNESCO Ethics Office governs staff conduct. Handbook: https://unesdoc.unesco.org/ark:/48223/pf0000386038. Governed primarily by ICSC Standards with agency-specific guidance. 2021 Ethics Office Annual Report noted plans for UNESCO-specific Code of Conduct. CROSS-LISTING from P (Education) and O.

records.document_title: WTO Rules of Conduct for the Dispute Settlement Understanding
records.profession_name: WTO Panel Member / Arbitrator / Secretariat Staff
records.notes: Applies to panel members, Appellate Body members, experts, arbitrators, and WTO Secretariat staff in dispute settlement. WTO Ethics, Risk, and Compliance Office established September 2024 for broader staff ethics. General staff conduct governed by international civil service norms. Narrower scope than other UN system ethics codes.
